chapters.n: The Lord himself opens his preface to the Book of Commandments by calling his church and all people everywhere to listen. It was given in November 1831 at a conference in Hiram, Ohio, which decided to publish Joseph Smith’s revelations.

f.g: listen carefully and obey.

chapters.n: The Lord’s message is for everyone; no one will escape hearing it. Eventually every eye will see and every heart will be touched by his word.

f.w: there is no eye that shall not see

chapters.n: Those who rebel will experience deep sorrow, because their sins — even secret ones — will be exposed publicly. Nothing hidden stays hidden from God.
God will warn the world through his chosen disciples in these last days. Missionary work is described as a “voice of warning” spoken in love.
No one will be able to stop these messengers, because the Lord himself has sent them.

f.g: stay = stop or hold back.

chapters.n: The Lord declares this revelation to be his own preface to the “book of my commandments” — the first published collection of Joseph Smith’s revelations, which later became the Doctrine and Covenants.

f.w: my preface unto the book of my commandments
f.g: The Book of Commandments was being printed in Independence, Missouri, in 1833 when a mob destroyed the press; the revelations were later published as the Doctrine and Covenants (1835).

chapters.n: Everything the Lord has decreed in these revelations will be fulfilled, so people should approach them with reverent awe.

f.g: here, reverent awe before God’s word, not terror.

chapters.n: Those who carry this message receive power to “seal” — to bind with heaven’s authority — including bearing witness against those who reject it.

f.w: power given to seal both on earth and in heaven

chapters.n: This sealing reserves the unbelieving for the day God’s judgment falls fully on the wicked.

f.g: without limit; in full.

chapters.n: When the Lord comes, he will reward everyone according to their deeds, and measure to each person the way they treated others.

f.g: repay; give back what is deserved.

f.w: according to the measure which he has measured to his fellow man

chapters.n: The Lord’s voice reaches the whole earth so that all who are willing to listen may hear.

f.w: all that will hear may hear

chapters.n: A simple and urgent message: get ready, because the Lord’s coming is near.

f.g: near.

chapters.n: Using Isaiah’s imagery, the Lord describes his sword as already prepared in heaven, ready to fall in judgment on the wicked.

f.w: his sword is bathed in heaven

chapters.n: The Lord’s power will be openly shown. Those who refuse to listen to him, his servants, or his prophets and apostles will be cut off from his people.

f.w: the arm of the Lord shall be revealed
shall be cut off from among the people

chapters.n: The reason for judgment: people have departed from God’s ordinances and broken his everlasting covenant — a description of the apostasy that preceded the Restoration.
Instead of seeking God, people follow their own ways and invent gods in the image of the world — idols of wealth and worldliness that will perish with “Babylon,” the symbol of a wicked world.

f.w: every man walketh in his own way
Babylon the great, which shall fall

chapters.n: Knowing the calamities ahead, the Lord called Joseph Smith, spoke to him from heaven, and gave him commandments. The Restoration was God’s answer to coming troubles.

f.w: called upon my servant Joseph Smith, Jun.

chapters.n: The Lord also commanded others to proclaim these truths, fulfilling ancient prophecies.
God uses the “weak things of the world” — humble, ordinary people — to accomplish great work, so people will not rely on human wisdom or the “arm of flesh.”

f.w: The weak things of the world

f.g: human strength alone, as opposed to God’s power.

chapters.n: The goal is that every person might speak in the name of the Lord, the Savior of the world — not just a privileged few.

f.w: every man might speak in the name of God the Lord

chapters.n: Another purpose of the Restoration: to increase faith throughout the earth.
God also intends to re-establish his everlasting covenant, the one that had been broken.
The fulness of the gospel will be preached by simple, ordinary people to the ends of the world, even to kings and rulers.
God affirms these revelations are his, given to imperfect servants in their own language so they could understand. Revelation is adapted to human limits.

f.w: after the manner of their language

chapters.n: Revelations also corrected the servants when they made mistakes. God openly acknowledges his prophets are not perfect.
When they sought wisdom, God taught them.
When they sinned, he disciplined them so they could repent. Several early revelations contain direct rebukes of Joseph and others.

f.g: corrected or disciplined for the purpose of improvement.

chapters.n: When they were humble, God made them strong and gave them knowledge line upon line, over time.
After receiving the Nephite record, Joseph Smith translated the Book of Mormon by God’s mercy and power, not by his own learning.

The Lord calls this church “the only true and living church” on earth, brought out of obscurity and darkness. He is pleased with the church as a whole, while not overlooking individual members’ faults.

f.w: out of obscurity and out of darkness
speaking unto the church collectively and not individually
f.g: the praise applies to the church as an institution, not as approval of every member’s conduct.

chapters.n: The Lord cannot accept sin in the least degree. His holiness is complete.

f.w: cannot look upon sin with the least degree of allowance

chapters.n: Yet anyone who repents and keeps the commandments will be forgiven. God’s holiness and mercy go together.

f.w: he that repents and does the commandments of the Lord shall be forgiven

chapters.n: Those who refuse to repent will lose even the light they already have, for God’s Spirit will not keep striving with them forever.

f.w: my Spirit shall not always strive with man

f.g: a title meaning Lord of the heavenly armies.

chapters.n: The Lord is willing to make these things known to everyone on earth.
God plays no favorites. He warns that the time is near — though not yet here — when peace will be taken from the earth and the devil will have power over his own domain.

f.w: peace shall be taken from the earth

chapters.n: The Lord will also reign among his Saints and come in judgment upon “Idumea,” here explained as a name for the world.

f.g: Greek form of Edom, Israel’s ancient enemy; used here as a symbol for the wicked world.

chapters.n: The Lord invites people to study these revelations, promising that every prophecy and promise in them will be fulfilled.
God does not take back his word. Whether he speaks himself or through his servants, it is the same, and it will all be fulfilled.

f.w: my word shall not pass away
whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants, it is the same

chapters.n: The preface closes with a testimony: the Lord is God, the Spirit witnesses of it, and this truth lasts forever.

On the night of September 21, 1823, the angel Moroni quoted Malachi to young Joseph Smith with an important difference: Elijah would “reveal the Priesthood” — the sealing power — before the Second Coming. Elijah restored these keys in the Kirtland Temple in 1836.

f.w: by the hand of Elijah the prophet
great and dreadful day of the Lord
f.g: the Second Coming — great for the righteous, dreadful for the wicked.

chapters.n: Elijah’s mission plants in the hearts of the living the promises God made to their ancestors, turning their hearts toward them. Latter-day Saints see this fulfilled in family history and temple work for the dead.

f.w: the promises made to the fathers
f.g: the covenant blessings promised to ancient patriarchs such as Abraham, including eternal family ties.

f.w: the hearts of the children shall turn to their fathers

chapters.n: Without this sealing link between generations, the earth would fail its purpose and be “utterly wasted” at Christ’s coming. Malachi says “smite the earth with a curse”; Moroni’s wording stresses that the purpose of creation would be lost.

f.g: completely ruined; left without its intended purpose.

chapters.n: In July 1828, after Martin Harris lost 116 pages of the Book of Mormon translation, the Lord opens this rebuke with reassurance: God’s plans cannot be defeated. This is the earliest of Joseph Smith’s written revelations that we have.

f.g: cannot be blocked or defeated.

chapters.n: God never takes crooked paths or wavers from his word. His course is “one eternal round” — consistent, unchanging, and dependable.

f.w: his course is one eternal round

chapters.n: The repeated “remember, remember” signals importance: it is human plans that fail, never God’s.
Even someone with many revelations and great spiritual power will fall if he boasts in his own strength and ignores God’s counsel to follow his own desires. Gifts don’t replace obedience.

f.g: worldly, fleshly wants.
treats as worthless; disregards.

chapters.n: The Lord reminds Joseph how strict his instructions had been about protecting the sacred record, and of the promises tied to obeying them.
Joseph had repeatedly given in to human persuasion — Martin Harris asked three times to take the manuscript, and Joseph finally let him.
The core problem: Joseph feared man more than God. Even when others disregard God’s counsel, a servant of God must not.

f.w: you should not have feared man more than God

chapters.n: Had Joseph stayed faithful, God would have protected him from the adversary’s attacks and stood with him in every trouble.
The Lord speaks directly: Joseph was chosen for this work, but if he doesn’t become aware of his transgression, he will fall.
Here is the hope in this revelation: God is merciful. If Joseph repents, he is still chosen and called again to the work.
If Joseph does not repent, he will lose his gift and become like any other man.
By giving up the manuscript, Joseph placed something sacred into the hands of a man who was not worthy of it.
Martin Harris had broken solemn promises, relied on his own judgment, and boasted of his wisdom. He later repented and became one of the Three Witnesses.

f.g: Martin had promised to show the pages only to a few family members.

chapters.n: Because of this, Joseph temporarily lost his privileges: the plates and interpreters were taken from him for a time.

f.g: for a period of time; temporarily.

chapters.n: From the beginning Joseph had allowed the counsel of his “director” — God — to be disregarded by repeatedly asking to let Martin take the pages.

f.g: God, who directed Joseph; some read it as the guidance Joseph received through the interpreters.
allowed.

chapters.n: Despite this setback, God’s work will move forward. Just as the Jews’ testimony (the Bible) brought knowledge of the Savior to the world, the Nephite record will bring it to their descendants.
The Book of Mormon will reach the descendants of the Nephite family groups — Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites — through their ancestors’ testimony.

f.w: the Nephites, and the Jacobites, and the Josephites, and the Zoramites

chapters.n: It will also reach the Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites, whose ancestors fell into unbelief and whom the Lord allowed to destroy the Nephites because of Nephite wickedness.

f.w: the Lamanites, and the Lemuelites, and the Ishmaelites

f.g: gradually declined in faith.

chapters.n: The plates were preserved precisely to fulfill God’s promises to his people.

f.w: for this very purpose are these plates preserved

chapters.n: The purpose: that the Lamanites will learn of their ancestors and God’s promises, believe the gospel, rely on Christ, and be saved through faith and repentance. This echoes the Book of Mormon’s title page.

f.w: rely upon the merits of Jesus Christ
come to the knowledge of their fathers

chapters.n: Given in February 1829 to Joseph Smith Sr., who had come to Harmony to visit his son. The Lord announces that a “marvelous work” — the Restoration and the Book of Mormon — is about to begin.
Anyone who joins in God’s service should give him everything — heart, might, mind, and strength — so they can stand blameless at the final judgment. This verse is often memorized by missionaries.

f.g: to set out on a journey or undertaking, like boarding a ship.

f.w: with all your heart, might, mind and strength

chapters.n: The simple qualification for being called: a desire to serve God. Desire is the starting point of discipleship.

f.w: if ye have desires to serve God ye are called to the work

chapters.n: Using harvest imagery, the Lord says the field is ripe — people are ready for the gospel. Those who work hard to gather souls also secure their own salvation.

f.w: the field is white already to harvest

f.g: begins harvesting with full effort; a sickle is a curved blade for cutting grain.

chapters.n: Faith, hope, charity, and love — with motives focused purely on God’s glory — are what truly qualify someone for this work, more than talent or education.

f.w: an eye single to the glory of God
f.g: a focus fixed only on God’s purposes, without selfish motives.

chapters.n: A list of Christlike attributes to remember, much like Peter’s list in his second epistle. These are qualities to develop over a lifetime.

f.g: self-control and moderation.

f.w: faith, virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, brotherly kindness, godliness, charity

chapters.n: The revelation closes with Jesus’ promise: ask and you will receive, knock and the door will open. God responds to sincere seeking.
In March 1829 Martin Harris, still wanting proof after losing the 116 pages, asked for a witness that Joseph truly had the plates. The Lord answers through Joseph.

f.g: a prosperous Palmyra farmer who financed the printing of the Book of Mormon and became one of the Three Witnesses.

chapters.n: Joseph is to tell Martin that the Lord gave him the plates and commanded him to be a witness of them.

f.w: stand as a witness of these things

chapters.n: Joseph had covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord designated, and he had no power over them except what God granted.

f.w: you should not show them except to those persons to whom I commanded you

chapters.n: Translating was Joseph’s first gift, and he was to focus on it alone, claiming no other gift until the translation was finished.

f.g: “pretend” here means to claim or lay claim to, not to fake.

chapters.n: Sorrow will come to the world if people refuse to listen to the Lord’s words.
Joseph will later be ordained and sent to deliver God’s word. This came true when he received the priesthood a few months later.
If people won’t believe God’s word, they wouldn’t believe Joseph even if he could show them the plates. Physical evidence doesn’t create faith.

f.w: if they will not believe my words, they would not believe you

chapters.n: The Lord expresses displeasure with an unbelieving, stubborn generation.

f.g: stubborn and proud, like an ox that refuses to bend its neck to the yoke.

chapters.n: The plates themselves are being kept back for a wise purpose and will be made known to future generations.
This generation will receive God’s word through Joseph’s translation rather than through seeing the plates.
Three other servants will be called to see the plates and testify along with Joseph. These became the Three Witnesses: Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris.

f.w: the testimony of three of my servants

chapters.n: Their certainty will come from heaven itself — God will declare the truth to them.

f.w: from heaven will I declare it unto them

chapters.n: God will give these witnesses the power to see the plates as they really are.

No one else in this generation will receive this same witness as the church emerges “out of the wilderness.” The poetic phrases describe the church’s beauty and strength, drawn from the Song of Solomon.

f.w: clear as the moon, and fair as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners

chapters.n: God repeats that he will send forth his word with the testimony of three witnesses.
Everyone who believes God’s words will receive the Spirit’s witness and be born again through baptism of water and of the Spirit. Personal revelation is available to all, not just the witnesses.

f.w: born of me, even of water and of the Spirit

chapters.n: A brief aside: Joseph must wait a little longer, because he has not yet been ordained.
The witnesses’ testimony will also stand as condemnation against those who harden their hearts.
A “desolating scourge” — widespread calamity — will repeatedly afflict the earth if people do not repent, until the wicked are consumed at Christ’s coming.

f.g: a devastating affliction or plague.

chapters.n: Just as the Lord warned the people of Jerusalem of their destruction and it came true, these warnings will also be fulfilled.
The Lord commands Joseph to repent, live more uprightly, and stop yielding to other people’s pressure — a clear reference to the lost manuscript episode.

f.w: yield to the persuasions of men no more

chapters.n: If Joseph stays firm in keeping the commandments, he is promised eternal life — even if he should be killed. This promise foreshadows his martyrdom in 1844.

f.w: even if you should be slain

chapters.n: The Lord returns to Martin Harris, the man asking for a witness.
Martin is too proud and has not humbled himself enough. But if he will bow down in sincere, mighty prayer, he will see what he desires — which happened in June 1829.
Then Martin can testify that he saw the things shown to Joseph by God’s power, not man’s.

f.w: by the power of God and not of man
f.g: The Testimony of Three Witnesses in the Book of Mormon uses similar language.

chapters.n: Martin’s testimony should be simple and limited: he has seen them by God’s power. Nothing more.
If Martin denies this testimony, he will break his covenant and be condemned.
Unless Martin humbles himself, admits his wrongs, covenants to keep the commandments, and exercises faith, he will not receive this vision.
If Martin will not humble himself, Joseph should tell him to stop pressing the Lord on this matter.
In that case, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then pause until the Lord commands him to resume.

f.w: thou shalt stop for a season

chapters.n: If Joseph disobeys, he will lose his gift and the sacred things entrusted to him.

f.w: thou shalt have no more gift

chapters.n: The Lord foresees enemies plotting against Joseph, and warns that Martin will fall into transgression if he doesn’t humble himself and receive the witness.

f.w: lying in wait to destroy thee

chapters.n: Many seek Joseph’s life. These commandments are given to protect him and prolong his days.
“Stop, and stand still” — the Lord will provide a way for Joseph to accomplish the work. God’s timing and means will be sufficient.
If Joseph remains faithful, he will be lifted up at the last day — exalted in God’s presence.

f.w: lifted up at the last day

chapters.n: Given in April 1829 shortly after Oliver Cowdery, a schoolteacher, arrived in Harmony and began serving as Joseph’s scribe. The Lord opens by announcing the great work about to unfold.
God’s word is living and powerful, sharper than any sword, cutting to the deepest part of a person. Oliver is told to take it seriously.

f.w: quick and powerful, sharper than a two-edged sword

f.g: alive, living.
apart; into separate pieces.

chapters.n: The harvest image again: the world is ready, and whoever wants to reap souls should work with all their might while there is time, laying up eternal salvation.

f.w: the field is white already to harvest

chapters.n: Anyone willing to work in the harvest is called of God.
Ask and receive; knock and it will be opened. The Lord repeats this promise often to early Church members.

f.w: if you will ask of me you shall receive

chapters.n: Since Oliver asked, the Lord tells him to keep the commandments and help establish Zion — a holy community of God’s people.

f.g: the work of building a righteous, unified people of God.

chapters.n: Seek wisdom instead of riches; then God’s mysteries will open to you, and you will be truly rich. Eternal life is the greatest wealth.

f.w: Seek not for riches but for wisdom

f.g: truths known only by revelation.

chapters.n: God will grant Oliver according to his desires. If he wishes, he can do much good in his generation.

f.w: even as you desire of me so it shall be unto you

chapters.n: Oliver’s message should center on repentance, and he should help bring forth God’s work.

f.w: Say nothing but repentance unto this generation

chapters.n: Oliver has a spiritual gift; he is reminded it is sacred and comes from God. D&C 8 later describes it as the gift of revelation and of working with the “rod.”
If Oliver inquires, he will learn great mysteries and can use his gift to bring many to the truth.
Oliver should share his gift only with those who share his faith, and must not treat sacred things lightly.

f.g: to treat carelessly or as unimportant.

chapters.n: If Oliver does good and endures faithfully, he will be saved — and salvation is the greatest of all God’s gifts.

f.w: there is no gift greater than the gift of salvation

chapters.n: The Lord commends Oliver for inquiring. Every time he asked, the Spirit instructed him — and that is how he came to be where he is.
Oliver had asked God and received enlightenment; the Lord now confirms that it came from the Spirit of truth.
Only God knows a person’s private thoughts and intentions — so this revelation’s knowledge of Oliver’s experience is itself a witness.

f.w: none else save God that knowest thy thoughts

chapters.n: The Lord witnesses to Oliver that the work he has been writing as scribe — the Book of Mormon translation — is true.
Oliver is to be diligent and stand loyally by Joseph through every hardship that comes for the sake of God’s word.
Oliver and Joseph should correct each other kindly when needed. The Lord also asks Oliver to be patient, serious, self-controlled, and full of faith, hope, and charity.

f.g: to warn or counsel gently but firmly.
serious-minded; thoughtful.
moderate; self-controlled.

chapters.n: Calling him by name, the Lord tells Oliver to treasure these words and promises to encircle him in the arms of his love.

f.w: encircle thee in the arms of my love

chapters.n: The speaker identifies himself: Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who came to his own people and was rejected, the light shining in darkness.

f.w: I am the same that came unto mine own, and mine own received me not

f.g: understands; can also mean overcomes or grasps.

chapters.n: If Oliver wants further witness, he should think back to the night he prayed in his heart about the truth of the work — something he had told no one.
God spoke peace to Oliver’s mind then. What greater witness could there be than one from God himself? Peace is a key way the Spirit testifies.

f.w: Did I not speak peace to your mind

chapters.n: Since the Lord has revealed things only Oliver knew, Oliver has received a true witness.

f.g: Oliver had told no one of that prayer, per Joseph Smith’s history.

chapters.n: The Lord offers Oliver the gift to translate as Joseph does, if he desires it. Oliver’s attempt is addressed in D&C 8 and 9.

f.w: a gift, if you desire of me, to translate

chapters.n: There are other records containing much of Christ’s gospel that have been held back because of human wickedness.

f.w: records which contain much of my gospel

chapters.n: If Oliver has righteous desires — to store up treasures in heaven — he may help bring hidden scripture to light.

f.w: lay up treasures for yourself in heaven

chapters.n: Joseph and Oliver are given the “keys” of this gift. Two or more witnesses establish truth, a biblical principle.

f.w: in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established

chapters.n: If people reject their message, Joseph and Oliver are still blessed; their enemies can do no more to them than was done to Christ.
Even if they are treated as Christ was, they will dwell with him in glory.
If people accept the message, they will be blessed, and Joseph and Oliver will rejoice in the fruit of their work.

f.w: joy in the fruit of your labors

chapters.n: Echoing his words in Matthew, Christ promises to be with those gathered in his name — and he is with Joseph and Oliver now.

f.w: where two or three are gathered together in my name

f.g: united in purpose; agreed about the same matter.

chapters.n: Don’t be afraid to do good. We reap what we sow, so sowing good brings good in return.

f.w: whatsoever ye sow, that shall ye also reap

chapters.n: “Fear not, little flock”: even if earth and hell unite against them, they cannot prevail if built on Christ’s rock.
Echoing his words to the woman in John 8, the Lord tells them he does not condemn them; they should sin no more and do their work seriously.

f.w: go your ways and sin no more

f.g: seriousness and earnestness.

chapters.n: One of the best-loved verses in the D&C: turn to Christ in every thought; don’t doubt, don’t fear.

f.w: Look unto me in every thought

chapters.n: The risen Christ invites them to consider the wounds in his side, hands, and feet — the proof of his atoning sacrifice — and promises the kingdom to the faithful.

f.w: the prints of the nails in my hands and feet

chapters.n: Joseph and Oliver disagreed about whether the Apostle John had died. Through the Urim and Thummim they received this translated version of a record John himself wrote, in which John recounts Jesus asking what he most desired.

f.g: John the Apostle, often called “the disciple whom Jesus loved.”

f.w: if you shall ask what you will, it shall be granted unto you

chapters.n: John asks for power over death so he can keep living and bringing souls to Christ — the same wish later granted to three Nephite disciples.
Because of this desire, John will “tarry” — remain on earth — until Christ comes in glory, prophesying to every nation and people.

f.g: remain; stay behind.

f.w: prophesy before nations, kindreds, tongues and people

chapters.n: This explains Jesus’ cryptic words to Peter in John 21: “If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?” John wanted to bring souls to Christ; Peter wanted to come quickly to Christ’s kingdom.

f.w: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?

chapters.n: Jesus assures Peter that his desire was good, but John chose to do an even greater work among people.
John will be like flaming fire and a ministering angel, serving those on earth who will inherit salvation.

f.w: as flaming fire and a ministering angel

chapters.n: Peter will minister alongside John and his brother James, holding the keys of this ministry until Christ comes. Peter, James, and John later restored the Melchizedek Priesthood to Joseph and Oliver.

f.w: unto you three I will give this power and the keys of this ministry

chapters.n: Both Peter and John receive what they desired, and both rejoice in their choices. God honors different righteous desires.

f.w: ye shall both have according to your desires

chapters.n: Oliver Cowdery wanted to translate too. The Lord promises that as surely as he lives, Oliver will gain knowledge of ancient records if he asks in faith with an honest heart.

f.w: ask in faith, with an honest heart

chapters.n: A key verse on how revelation works: God speaks to both the mind (thoughts and understanding) and the heart (feelings) through the Holy Ghost.

f.w: I will tell you in your mind and in your heart

chapters.n: This is the spirit of revelation — the same power by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. Even dramatic miracles were guided by quiet inspiration.

f.w: through the Red Sea on dry ground

chapters.n: Revelation is Oliver’s gift. If he uses it, it will protect him from enemies who would destroy him.

f.g: give diligent attention to it; put it to use.

chapters.n: The Lord urges Oliver to remember these words and keep the commandments, repeating: this is your gift.
Oliver has another gift, the “gift of Aaron.” Earlier versions called it a gift of working with a rod; Aaron’s rod in Exodus was a tool through which God showed his power.

f.g: The 1833 Book of Commandments called this “the gift of working with the rod.” Its exact nature is not fully known.

chapters.n: Only God’s power can make this gift work. It is not magic but divine help.
Oliver should not doubt, since the gift is from God. He will hold it in his hands and do marvelous works, and no one can take it from him.
Whatever Oliver asks to know through this means, the Lord will tell him.
Faith is essential — without it nothing can be done. Oliver must not treat sacred things lightly or ask for inappropriate things.

f.w: without faith you can do nothing

chapters.n: Oliver should ask to understand God’s mysteries and to translate sacred hidden records. It will be done according to his faith.

f.w: according to your faith shall it be done unto you

chapters.n: The Lord affirms he is the same one who has spoken to Oliver from the beginning — including the private answer recalled in D&C 6.

f.w: I am the same that spake unto you from the beginning

chapters.n: Oliver tried to translate but did not succeed, and went back to being Joseph’s scribe. The Lord tenderly calls him “my son” and asks him to keep writing until the Book of Mormon is finished.

f.g: a term of affection and covenant relationship, not a rebuke.

chapters.n: Oliver will have power to help translate other records in the future.
Oliver should be patient; it isn’t wise for him to translate right now.

f.g: suitable or advisable at the time.

chapters.n: His present calling is to be Joseph’s scribe — important work in its own right.
Oliver lost the privilege because he didn’t continue as he had begun.
Oliver should not complain; the Lord has handled this wisely.

f.g: to grumble or complain quietly.

chapters.n: Oliver’s mistake: he assumed God would simply hand him the translation when all he did was ask. Revelation usually requires effort on our part.

f.w: you took no thought save it was to ask me

chapters.n: A central teaching on personal revelation: study it out in your mind, reach a conclusion, then ask God if it is right. If it is, he will cause your bosom to “burn” — a feeling of confirmation.

f.w: study it out in your mind
your bosom shall burn within you

chapters.n: If it is not right, you will feel no such confirmation but a “stupor of thought” — a confused, foggy feeling that makes the wrong idea slip away.

f.g: mental dullness or confusion; an inability to hold onto the idea.

chapters.n: Had Oliver understood this process, he could have translated — but now is not the time.
The opportunity was right when he began, but fear got in the way, and the moment has passed.
Joseph has been given enough strength to carry on, so the work is not harmed. The Lord gently adds that he condemns neither of them.

f.w: neither of you have I condemned

chapters.n: If Oliver does what he’s been asked, he will prosper. He must stay faithful and resist temptation.
Stand firm in your calling, and not a hair of your head will be lost; you will be lifted up at the last day.

f.w: a hair of your head shall not be lost
lifted up at the last day

chapters.n: The Lord reviews what happened with the 116 manuscript pages: Joseph gave the writings he translated through the Urim and Thummim to Martin Harris, and they were lost. Most historians now date this revelation to spring 1829, though parts may reflect 1828.

f.g: Hebrew, often rendered “lights and perfections”; sacred instruments used to receive revelation and translate.

chapters.n: Joseph lost his gift at the same time, and his mind was darkened — a vivid description of spiritual loss.
But now the gift has been restored. Joseph is to remain faithful and finish the translation he began.

f.w: it is now restored unto you again

chapters.n: Wise counsel: don’t work faster or harder than your strength and resources allow, but be steady and diligent to the end. Balance is part of faithfulness.

f.w: Do not run faster or labor more than you have strength

chapters.n: Constant prayer is the key to overcoming Satan and escaping those who serve him.

f.g: emerge victorious.

chapters.n: Enemies have tried to destroy Joseph — even someone he trusted, Martin Harris, had worked against him by giving up the manuscript.
Martin is called wicked here because his actions threatened the sacred trust and Joseph’s gift. He later repented and was called as a witness.
Because the pages were handed to Martin, wicked men were able to take them.
In effect, Joseph had delivered something sacred into wicked hands.
Satan has inspired those who took the pages to change the words that Joseph translated.

f.g: to change the text so it no longer matches the original translation.

chapters.n: Because the words are altered, the stolen manuscript now reads differently from what Joseph dictated.
This is the devil’s cunning plan to destroy the work.

f.g: clever in a deceptive or scheming way.

chapters.n: The plotters hope to catch Joseph in an apparent contradiction and claim he is a fraud.

f.g: here in the plotters’ mouths: claimed falsely to translate.

chapters.n: The Lord will not allow Satan’s plan to succeed.

f.g: allow, permit.

chapters.n: Satan wants Joseph to “tempt the Lord” by asking to retranslate the same material.
The plotters reason: if God really gave Joseph power to translate, he’ll be able to do it again.
If Joseph produces the same words, they will compare it against their altered copy.
Since the versions won’t match, they’ll claim Joseph lied and has no gift.
Their goal is to destroy Joseph and the work, avoid being shamed, and gain worldly praise.
Satan holds a strong grip on their hearts and stirs them against goodness.
Their hearts are corrupt; like those described in John’s Gospel, they love darkness rather than light because their deeds are evil, so they won’t ask God.

f.w: they love darkness rather than light, because their deeds are evil

chapters.n: Satan’s purpose in stirring them up is to lead their souls to destruction.
God will hold the plotters accountable; their scheme will end in their own shame at the judgment.

f.w: I will require this at their hands
f.g: I will hold them responsible.

chapters.n: Satan stirs up anger against the work of God.
Satan flatters people into thinking it’s no sin to lie in order to trap someone they think is lying. Deception justified by a “good cause” is still deception.

f.g: praises falsely to manipulate.

chapters.n: He leads them along with flattery until he drags them down — they end up caught in their own trap.

f.w: catch themselves in their own snare

chapters.n: Satan roams the earth seeking to destroy souls — language borrowed from the book of Job.

f.w: he goeth up and down, to and fro in the earth

chapters.n: Woe to anyone who lies to deceive just because they suspect someone else is lying. God’s justice applies to them too.
Satan persuades them that Joseph has deceived them, which flatters them into wickedness and into tempting God through Joseph.
The Lord’s command: do not retranslate the lost portion.
If Joseph produced the same words, the plotters would claim he contradicted himself and was faking.
They would publish the supposed contradiction, and Satan would turn people against Joseph so they would reject God’s word.
Satan’s aim is to overpower Joseph’s testimony and stop the work from coming forth in this generation.
The Lord gives wise instructions, and Joseph should keep them private until the translation is finished.
Joseph shouldn’t be surprised at this caution — it is for his own protection.
This doesn’t mean he can never share it with righteous people.
But since Joseph cannot always tell the righteous from the wicked, he should stay quiet until the Lord decides to reveal everything.

f.g: keep silent.

chapters.n: Here is the solution: the events covered in the lost pages are also recorded on the “plates of Nephi” — the small plates Mormon included with his abridgment.
The lost manuscript itself had mentioned that a more detailed account was on Nephi’s plates.
Nephi’s account is more focused on spiritual things the Lord wants the people to know.

f.g: more detailed, especially on spiritual matters.

chapters.n: Joseph is to translate the small plates of Nephi, covering the same period up to King Benjamin’s reign, where the retained translation picks up.
This becomes the record of Nephi — what we know as 1 Nephi through Omni — confounding those who altered the words.

f.g: to confuse or defeat; to frustrate someone’s plans.

chapters.n: God’s wisdom is greater than the devil’s cunning. Centuries earlier, Nephi and Mormon were inspired to prepare this backup plan.

f.w: my wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil

chapters.n: The thieves have only part of the account — Mormon’s abridgment of the large plates.

f.g: a shortened version or summary.

chapters.n: Nephi’s small plates contain many teachings that shed greater light on the gospel, so it is wise to include them.

f.w: throw greater views upon my gospel

chapters.n: The rest of the Book of Mormon contains the gospel teachings that ancient prophets and disciples prayed would reach their people’s descendants.
The Lord promised to grant their prayers according to their faith.
They prayed that the gospel would reach the Lamanites and those who had joined them through dissension.

f.g: disagreements that caused people to break away.

chapters.n: They also prayed that the gospel would reach other nations who might later inhabit the land.

f.w: other nations should possess this land

chapters.n: They left a blessing on the land: whoever believes this gospel here may have eternal life.
This blessing is free to every nation, kindred, tongue, and people.
God will bring forth this part of his gospel in answer to their faith — not to replace what people have (the Bible) but to build it up.

f.w: to destroy that which they have received, but to build it up

chapters.n: If this generation does not harden its heart, the Lord will establish his church among them. The Church was organized in April 1830.

f.w: I will establish my church among them

chapters.n: The aim is to build, not destroy, the Lord’s church.
Those who truly belong to Christ’s church need not fear; they will inherit heaven.
But those who don’t fear God, who build churches for profit, or who build the devil’s kingdom will be shaken to the core.

f.w: build up churches unto themselves to get gain

chapters.n: The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ, rejected by his own people.

f.w: I came unto mine own, and mine own received me not

chapters.n: He is the light shining in darkness, which the darkness does not grasp.

f.w: I am the light which shineth in darkness

chapters.n: Christ recalls telling his disciples about “other sheep” — words many did not understand. The Book of Mormon explains that he meant the Nephites.

f.w: Other sheep have I which are not of this fold

chapters.n: He will show that these other sheep were a branch of the house of Jacob (Israel).

f.w: a branch of the house of Jacob

chapters.n: He will reveal the marvelous works the Nephites did in his name.
The Book of Mormon will not contradict the Bible but support it, clarifying the true points of Christ’s doctrine.

f.w: the true points of my doctrine

chapters.n: The goal is to reduce contention over doctrine. Satan stirs up disputes, and people go wrong by twisting scriptures they don’t understand.

f.g: to twist or distort the meaning of.

chapters.n: The Lord will reveal to them this great mystery.
Using an image Jesus spoke over Jerusalem, he will gather his people like a hen gathering her chicks — if they don’t harden their hearts.

f.w: as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings

chapters.n: All who are willing may come and drink freely of the waters of life.
A clear definition: whoever repents and comes to Christ is his church. At its core, the church is a community of the repentant.

f.w: whosoever repenteth and cometh unto me, the same is my church

chapters.n: Anyone who teaches more or less than this core doctrine is not of Christ.
Those who endure in his church to the end will be built on his rock, and hell’s gates will not overcome them.

f.w: the gates of hell shall not prevail against them

chapters.n: Remember the words of the one who is the life and light of the world — your Redeemer, Lord, and God.

f.w: the life and light of the world

chapters.n: Joseph’s older brother Hyrum came to Harmony in May 1829 eager to help. The Lord begins with the same announcement given to Oliver: a marvelous work is about to come forth.
Hyrum is told, as Oliver was, that God’s word is living and piercing. Opening several revelations with the same words reminds each person that the same God is calling them.
Hyrum receives the harvest invitation: the world is ready, and those who labor with all their might store up eternal salvation.

f.w: the field is white already to harvest

chapters.n: The willingness to work in the harvest is itself a sign of God’s call.
Hyrum is assured that sincere asking and knocking will be answered.

f.w: if you will knock it shall be opened unto you

chapters.n: Hyrum’s first duties: obey the commandments and help build Zion.
True riches are wisdom and eternal life, not money. This is counsel Hyrum, a farmer of modest means, lived by faithfully.

f.w: he that hath eternal life is rich

chapters.n: The Lord will grant Hyrum’s righteous desires, and he can do much good in his generation.
Hyrum’s message should be repentance. He should obey and help bring forth the Lord’s work.
Here the revelation turns personal: Hyrum has a gift, or will have one if he asks in faith with an honest heart, trusting Christ’s power.
Christ confirms he is the one speaking, the light shining in darkness.

f.w: the light which shineth in darkness

chapters.n: A simple way to recognize the Spirit: it leads us to do good, act justly, walk humbly, and judge righteously. This echoes Micah’s famous summary of true religion.

f.w: to do justly, to walk humbly
that Spirit which leadeth to do good

chapters.n: The Spirit enlightens the mind and fills the soul with joy — two dependable signs of its influence.
Through the Spirit, Hyrum can know whatever righteous things he desires, if he asks in faith.
Hyrum shouldn’t assume he is called to preach until he is properly called. Authority to preach comes through God’s order.
Wait a little longer — until the Book of Mormon (“my word”), the gospel, and the Church are in place, so Hyrum can know the doctrine with certainty.

f.w: my word, my rock, my church, and my gospel

chapters.n: Then his desires and faith will be fulfilled.
In the meantime: keep the commandments, stay quiet, and rely on the Spirit.

f.g: be silent for now; don’t rush to preach.

chapters.n: Hyrum should cling to the Lord with all his heart and be patient while the translation is completed.
Hyrum’s work for now is simple but demanding: keep the commandments with all his might, mind, and strength.

f.w: with all your might, mind and strength

chapters.n: A widely quoted principle: before seeking to declare God’s word, first obtain it. Then the Lord will loosen your tongue, and the Spirit will give power to convince.

f.w: first seek to obtain my word

f.g: you will be able to speak freely and powerfully.

chapters.n: Hyrum should study the scriptures already available (the Bible) and those coming forth (the Book of Mormon being translated). Then more will be added.

f.g: the Book of Mormon, then in the process of translation.

chapters.n: Calling him by name, the Lord tells Hyrum to seek God’s kingdom first, and all else will be added justly.

f.w: seek the kingdom of God, and all things shall be added

chapters.n: Hyrum should build on Christ’s rock — his gospel.
Do not deny the spirit of revelation or prophecy; there is real danger in rejecting them.
Hyrum should treasure these teachings until the Lord’s time comes for him to go out. He would later serve faithfully as a leader and Patriarch.
This counsel applies to everyone with righteous desires who has begun to labor.
The Lord declares himself: Jesus Christ, the life and light of the world.

f.w: the life and the light of the world

chapters.n: He is the same one who came to his own people and was rejected.
But all who receive and believe in him are given power to become God’s sons and daughters — a promise quoted from John’s Gospel.

f.w: power to become the sons of God

chapters.n: Joseph Knight Sr., a friend from Colesville, New York, brought food and supplies so the translation could continue. In May 1829 he asked what the Lord wanted of him, and receives the same opening announcement given to others.
God’s word is described as powerful and piercing — reaching the deepest parts of the soul.
The harvest is ready; those who work hard in it secure their own salvation.

f.w: thrust in his sickle with his might

chapters.n: Joseph Knight is assured that anyone willing to reap is called of God.
God answers those who ask and knock.

f.w: ask of me you shall receive

chapters.n: Joseph Knight’s duty, like others’, is to keep the commandments and help establish Zion.
This counsel applies not only to Joseph Knight but to anyone who wants to help build the work.
The qualifications for helping are spiritual: humility, love, faith, hope, charity, and moderation in all responsibilities.
Christ, the light and life of the world, tells Joseph Knight to listen with all his might — and then he is called.

f.w: the light and the life of the world

chapters.n: On May 15, 1829, on the bank of the Susquehanna River, John the Baptist appeared as a resurrected messenger and conferred the Aaronic Priesthood on Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery. It holds the keys of angelic ministry, repentance, and baptism by immersion, and will remain on earth until the sons of Levi again offer a righteous offering.

f.g: John the Baptist speaks humbly as a co-worker, not a superior.

f.w: the sons of Levi do offer again an offering unto the Lord in righteousness

chapters.n: In June 1829 the translation moved to the Peter Whitmer Sr. farm in Fayette, New York. David Whitmer, who had helped bring Joseph and Oliver there, asks what he should do and hears the familiar opening words.
David is told to pay close attention to God’s word, which is living and penetrating.

f.w: the dividing asunder of both joints and marrow
f.g: an image of God’s word cutting to the innermost part of a person.

chapters.n: The harvest image calls David to labor while there is still daylight — while life and opportunity last.
Desire and willingness to work are what make David “called of God.”
The promise of answered prayer is repeated to David.

f.w: if you will knock it shall be opened unto you

chapters.n: David is to help build Zion and keep all the commandments.
Obedience and enduring to the end lead to eternal life, the greatest of all God’s gifts.

f.w: eternal life, which gift is the greatest of all the gifts of God

chapters.n: If David asks the Father in faith, he will receive the Holy Ghost to help him testify of what he will hear and see — a hint that he would become one of the Three Witnesses.

f.w: stand as a witness of the things of which you shall both hear and see

f.g: gives the ability to speak, providing the words.

chapters.n: Christ identifies himself as Creator of heaven and earth — a light that cannot be hidden.

f.w: who created the heavens and the earth
a light which cannot be hid in darkness

chapters.n: The fulness of the gospel will come forth through the Gentiles to the house of Israel — the reverse of its first spread, as Book of Mormon prophecy foretold.

f.w: from the Gentiles unto the house of Israel

chapters.n: David is called to assist; if faithful, he will be blessed spiritually and temporally. He later testified of the plates for the rest of his life, though he separated from the Church in 1838.

f.g: in matters of the spirit and in practical, earthly life.

chapters.n: John Whitmer, one of David’s brothers, helped as a scribe at Fayette in June 1829. Jesus Christ addresses him personally as his Lord and Redeemer.

f.g: John Whitmer, later a Church historian and one of the Eight Witnesses of the Book of Mormon plates.

chapters.n: The Lord speaks plainly and powerfully, because his authority reaches over the whole earth.

f.w: mine arm is over all the earth

f.g: directness and clarity.

chapters.n: Christ will reveal something only he and John know — a private witness that the revelation is genuine.

f.w: that which no man knoweth save me and thee alone

chapters.n: John had often prayed to know what would be most valuable for him to do with his life.
The Lord blesses John for asking and for sharing the words he has been given.
The answer: the thing of most worth is to call people to repentance and bring souls to Christ, so John can rest with them in the Father’s kingdom. Helping others come to Christ brings eternal joy.

f.w: rest with them in the kingdom of my Father

chapters.n: Peter Whitmer Jr., another Whitmer brother, received a revelation almost identical to his brother John’s. The near-identical wording shows God gives the same core counsel to each sincere seeker.

f.g: Peter Whitmer Jr., one of the Eight Witnesses; he later served a mission to the Lamanites in 1830–31.

chapters.n: Peter is reminded that Christ speaks with authority and power over all the earth.
As with John, the Lord tells Peter something no one else knows — the hidden desires of his heart.

f.w: no man knoweth save me and thee alone

chapters.n: Peter, too, had repeatedly asked what would be most valuable for him.
The Lord commends Peter for asking and for sharing God’s words as commanded.
The answer to Peter mirrors John’s: declare repentance and bring souls to Christ. For any disciple, this is work of supreme worth.

f.w: the thing which will be of the most worth unto you

chapters.n: In June 1829, Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris were promised that, by relying on God’s word with full purpose, they would see the plates and sacred objects connected with them — Laban’s sword, the breastplate, the Urim and Thummim, and the Liahona.

f.w: the Urim and Thummim, which were given to the brother of Jared
the miraculous directors which were given to Lehi
f.g: the Liahona, a compass-like ball that guided Lehi’s family.

chapters.n: They will see these things by faith — the same faith ancient prophets had.

f.w: that faith which was had by the prophets of old

chapters.n: After seeing with their own eyes, they must testify by God’s power. This became “The Testimony of Three Witnesses” printed in every Book of Mormon.
Their testimony would protect Joseph from being destroyed — he would no longer be the only witness — and further God’s purposes.
They will testify as Joseph does; Joseph saw by God’s power and because of his faith.
The Lord himself testifies that Joseph has translated the portion of the book he was commanded to translate, and that it is true — a striking divine endorsement.

f.w: as your Lord and your God liveth it is true

chapters.n: The three witnesses receive the same power, faith, and gift that Joseph had.
If they obey, hell’s gates will not prevail against them; Christ’s grace is enough for them, and they will be lifted up at the last day.

f.w: my grace is sufficient for you
the gates of hell shall not prevail against you

chapters.n: Jesus Christ seals this revelation with his own name, to fulfill his righteous purposes.
In June 1829, Oliver Cowdery wanted to know how to build up the Church. The Lord answers him (and later David Whitmer) in this revelation about the worth of souls and the calling of the Twelve.

f.g: Joseph’s scribe, co-recipient of the priesthood, and one of the Three Witnesses.

chapters.n: The Spirit has repeatedly witnessed to Oliver that what he wrote down — the Book of Mormon — is true.

f.w: the things which you have written are true

chapters.n: Since he knows it is true, Oliver must rely on what is written there as his guide.
The Book of Mormon contains everything needed about the foundation of Christ’s church, gospel, and rock.

f.w: the foundation of my church, my gospel, and my rock

chapters.n: If Oliver builds the church on this foundation, hell will not prevail against him.

f.w: the gates of hell shall not prevail

chapters.n: The world is ripening in wickedness, so people everywhere — Gentiles and Israel — must be stirred to repentance.

f.g: growing toward full readiness for judgment, as fruit ripens for harvest.

chapters.n: Joseph baptized Oliver as commanded, fulfilling his duty. (The two baptized each other on May 15, 1829, after receiving the Aaronic Priesthood.)

f.w: baptized by the hands of my servant Joseph Smith, Jun.

chapters.n: Don’t be surprised that God has called Joseph for his purposes. If Joseph stays diligent, he will receive eternal life.
God commands all people everywhere to repent. Oliver and David are called with the same calling as the Apostle Paul — a hint at apostleship.

f.w: I command all men everywhere to repent
even as unto Paul mine apostle

chapters.n: One of the most quoted verses in the D&C: the worth of souls is great in the sight of God. Every person matters infinitely to him.

f.w: the worth of souls is great

chapters.n: Why souls are so valuable: Christ died and suffered the pain of all people so that all could repent and come to him.

f.w: he suffered the pain of all men

chapters.n: He rose from the dead to bring all people to him, on the condition of repentance.
Christ rejoices greatly over every soul who repents.

f.w: how great is his joy in the soul that repenteth

chapters.n: So Oliver and David are called to cry repentance to their generation.
Even if they labored their whole lives and brought just one soul to Christ, their joy with that person in God’s kingdom would be great.

f.g: even if only one soul.

chapters.n: And if one soul brings great joy, how much greater the joy of bringing many!

f.w: how great will be your joy

chapters.n: They have the gospel, Christ’s rock, and his salvation before them.
Ask the Father in Christ’s name with faith, and the Holy Ghost will reveal all that people need to know.

f.w: the Holy Ghost, which manifesteth all things

chapters.n: Without faith, hope, and charity, nothing of eternal value can be done.
Do not fight against other churches, except the “church of the devil” — meaning everything that opposes God, not a single denomination.

f.g: In Nephi’s vision, a symbol of all that fights against God, not one specific church.

chapters.n: Take Christ’s name upon you and speak the truth seriously and soberly.

f.w: Take upon you the name of Christ

f.g: seriousness and self-control.

chapters.n: Those who repent, are baptized in Jesus’ name, and endure to the end will be saved — the doctrine of Christ in a single sentence.
Jesus Christ is the only name given by the Father through which people can be saved.

f.w: none other name given whereby man can be saved

chapters.n: Everyone must take this name, for it is the name by which they will be called at the last day.

f.w: in that name shall they be called at the last day

chapters.n: Those who don’t know the name they are called by cannot have a place in God’s kingdom.

f.w: know not the name by which they are called

chapters.n: Others will be called to preach the gospel to both Gentile and Jew.
There will be twelve, who will take Christ’s name with full purpose of heart. This foretells the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, organized in 1835.

f.g: complete and sincere commitment.

chapters.n: The Twelve are called to take the gospel to all the world and every creature.

f.w: preach my gospel unto every creature

chapters.n: They are ordained to baptize in Christ’s name according to the scriptures.
Oliver and David have the written guidance (the Book of Mormon) and must follow it.

f.w: you have that which is written before you

chapters.n: The Lord speaks directly to the future Twelve: his grace is sufficient, but they must walk uprightly and avoid sin.

f.w: my grace is sufficient for you

chapters.n: The Twelve will ordain priests and teachers and preach the gospel by the power of the Holy Ghost.
Jesus Christ affirms he has spoken these words.
These words come from Christ, not man, and Oliver and David must testify of that.
When they read these revelations, they are hearing Christ’s voice, given by his Spirit and power. This applies to anyone who reads scripture by the Spirit.

f.w: it is my voice which speaketh them unto you

chapters.n: So they can truly testify they have heard Christ’s voice and know his words.
Oliver and David are assigned to find the Twelve who have these righteous desires. In 1835 they, with Martin Harris, selected the first Quorum of the Twelve.

f.g: In February 1835 the Three Witnesses chose the first twelve apostles of this dispensation.

chapters.n: They will recognize the Twelve by their desires and works.

f.w: by their desires and their works you shall know them

chapters.n: When they find them, they are to share these instructions with them.
They are to humbly worship the Father in Christ’s name.

f.w: worship the Father in my name

chapters.n: Their message to the world: repent and be baptized in Jesus Christ’s name.

f.w: You must repent and be baptized

chapters.n: Everyone must repent and be baptized — men, women, and children who reach the age of accountability (later specified as eight years old).
After receiving this, they must keep all of God’s commandments.
Through them, God will do a marvelous work, convincing many of their sins and bringing them to repentance and his kingdom.
The blessings God gives them are above all else.
But if they receive all this and then don’t keep the commandments, they cannot be saved. Greater light brings greater responsibility.

f.w: if you keep not my commandments

chapters.n: The revelation closes with Christ’s own seal: spoken by the power of his Spirit.

Given to Martin Harris, likely in summer 1829, as he hesitated to mortgage his farm to pay for printing the Book of Mormon. Christ introduces himself as Alpha and Omega — the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet — the beginning and end of all things.

f.g: first and last letters of the Greek alphabet; Christ is the beginning and the end.

chapters.n: Christ has fully accomplished the Father’s will, including the Atonement, which gives him power to bring all things under his rule.

f.w: having accomplished and finished the will of him whose I am

chapters.n: He keeps all power, including power to destroy Satan’s works at the end and to judge everyone by their deeds on the great final day.

f.w: judging every man according to his works

chapters.n: A sobering principle: everyone must either repent or suffer. God is endless, and his law cannot be sidestepped.

f.w: every man must repent or suffer

chapters.n: God does not take back his judgments; sorrow awaits those found on his “left hand” at judgment — an image from Jesus’ parable of the sheep and goats.

f.g: grinding of teeth in anguish or regret.

chapters.n: A key clarification: scripture doesn’t say the torment has no end; it says “endless torment.” The Lord is about to explain the difference.
Likewise “eternal damnation” — such strong language was used to move people’s hearts toward repentance, for God’s glory.

f.g: more emphatic or forceful.

chapters.n: The Lord will explain this mystery to Martin, as he would to his apostles.

f.g: fitting, appropriate.

chapters.n: He speaks to those chosen for this work, united as one, so they may enter his rest.
Here is the mystery: “Endless” is one of God’s names. So “endless punishment” means punishment given by the Endless God — describing its source and kind, not necessarily its duration.
“Eternal punishment” means God’s punishment, since Eternal is also his name.
The same applies to “endless punishment.” This insight shows that God’s punishments are real yet purposeful, not merely infinite for the sake of it.
So Martin is commanded to repent and keep the commandments he received through Joseph Smith.
Those commandments came by God’s almighty power.
Christ pleads again: repent, lest suffering come that is more severe, intense, and hard to bear than Martin can imagine.

f.g: his word, which has power to judge.
here, extremely intense or acute.

chapters.n: One of the most important verses on the Atonement: Christ himself suffered these things for everyone, so that we need not suffer if we repent.

f.w: I, God, have suffered these things for all

chapters.n: But those who won’t repent must suffer as he did. The Atonement is freely offered but must be accepted.

f.w: they must suffer even as I

chapters.n: In the only first-person account of Gethsemane in scripture, Christ describes trembling with pain, bleeding from every pore, suffering in body and spirit, and wishing he could avoid the bitter cup.

Christ commands Martin again to repent and confess, reminding him that he had tasted a small portion of this suffering when the Spirit was withdrawn — likely after the loss of the 116 pages.

f.w: at the time I withdrew my Spirit

chapters.n: Martin should preach only repentance, and not share these deeper teachings with the world until the Lord sees fit.
People can’t yet handle “meat,” only “milk” — they must learn simple truths before deeper ones.

f.w: they cannot bear meat now, but milk they must receive

chapters.n: A tender invitation: learn of Christ, listen to his words, walk in the meekness of his Spirit, and you will find peace in him.

f.w: you shall have peace in me

chapters.n: Jesus Christ came by the Father’s will and does his will.

f.w: I came by the will of the Father

chapters.n: Martin must not covet another man’s wife or seek anyone’s life — echoing the Ten Commandments.

f.w: thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife

chapters.n: Martin must not covet even his own property, but give it freely to print the Book of Mormon. He later mortgaged his farm for $3,000 to pay the printer.

f.g: to cling selfishly to one’s own possessions when God asks for them.

chapters.n: The Book of Mormon goes first to the Gentiles and then to the Jews — including the Lamanites as a remnant of Israel — so they can believe and stop waiting for a Messiah who has already come.

f.w: my word to the Gentile, that soon it may go to the Jew

chapters.n: Martin should pray aloud as well as silently, both publicly and privately.

f.w: pray vocally as well as in thy heart

chapters.n: He should declare the good news everywhere he can, “upon the mountains” — a phrase from Isaiah about messengers of peace.
Do it humbly, trusting in the Lord, and without insulting those who insult you.

chapters.n: Don’t argue over “tenets” — disputed points of doctrine. Instead teach the basics: repentance, faith in Christ, and forgiveness through baptism and the Holy Ghost.

chapters.n: All this came by Christ’s grace, to whom all glory belongs.

entangled again in the vanities of the world

chapters.n: The Book of Mormon tells of a fallen people and contains the fulness of Christ’s gospel for Gentiles and Jews.

Christ was tempted but did not give in.

f.w: He suffered temptations but gave no heed unto them

chapters.n: He was crucified, died, and rose again on the third day.

chapters.n: All who believe, are baptized in his name, and endure in faith will be saved.

f.w: who truly testified of him in all things

chapters.n: God has spoken; honor and glory to his name.

f.w: willing to take upon them the name of Jesus Christ

chapters.n: Now the duties of priesthood holders and members are outlined. An apostle is also an elder and is called to baptize.

chapters.n: They encourage members to meet often and to do their duty.
Teachers lead meetings when no elder or priest is present.
Deacons assist teachers in their duties when needed.

f.w: invite all to come unto Christ

f.g: a gathering of Church leaders and members for instruction and business.

chapters.n: These conferences handle whatever Church business is necessary.
Elders receive licenses — written certificates of authority — from other elders by vote of their congregation or conference.

f.g: written certificates showing one’s ordination and authority.

Instructions for blessing the cup.

f.g: one who sees by divine power things hidden or yet to come.

f.w: the sixth day of the month which is called April

chapters.n: The Church must give heed to all the words and commandments the prophet receives, living in holiness.

cause the heavens to shake for your good

religious acts without divine authority or saving power.

clothing.

ye may be my people and I will be your God

chapters.n: Edward Partridge, recently called as the Church’s first bishop, is confirmed in that office. The Lord adds a warning that applies to any leader: if he falls into sin, someone else will be called.
No one may preach or organize the Church on his own initiative. He must be ordained by someone with authority, and the Church must know it. This protects members from self-appointed teachers.

f.w: ordained by some one who has authority

chapters.n: Teachers are to draw their lessons from the Bible and the Book of Mormon. The Book of Mormon is described as containing the fulness of the gospel—the basic doctrines needed for salvation.
They are also to follow the covenants and “articles” of the Church, likely meaning the founding document now found in D&C 20, while letting the Spirit guide how they teach.

f.g: The “Articles and Covenants” of the Church, now D&C 20, read at early conferences.

chapters.n: A key teaching principle: the Spirit comes through sincere, faith-filled prayer, and without the Spirit a person should not try to teach. Gospel teaching is spiritual work, not just information.

f.w: if ye receive not the Spirit ye shall not teach

chapters.n: These teaching rules apply until a fuller set of scriptures is given—likely a reference to Joseph Smith’s inspired revision of the Bible, then in progress.

f.g: Probably the Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible, which the Lord was then directing (see v. 56).

chapters.n: When elders speak under the influence of the Comforter (the Holy Ghost), they will say what the Lord wants said, even prophetically.
The reason the Holy Ghost can be trusted: he knows all things and testifies of the Father and the Son.

f.w: beareth record of the Father and of the Son

chapters.n: The Lord now turns from the elders to the whole Church and restates moral laws, starting with murder. Deliberate killing of the innocent is described as a sin without forgiveness in this life or the next.

f.w: shall not have forgiveness in this world, nor in the world to come

chapters.n: The command against murder is repeated, adding that a murderer forfeits his life—echoing the ancient law that the civil authorities would carry out (see v. 79).
Stealing is forbidden. A thief who will not repent is to be “cast out,” meaning removed from Church membership. The door of repentance is still implied.

f.g: Excommunicated—removed from membership in the Church.

chapters.n: Lying is likewise forbidden, with the same consequence for those who refuse to repent. Honesty is part of the foundation of Zion.
Marriage calls for whole-hearted love and complete loyalty. To “cleave” means to cling or hold fast—the same word used in Genesis for husband and wife becoming one.

f.w: cleave unto her and none else

chapters.n: Echoing the Sermon on the Mount, the Lord teaches that sin begins in the heart. Feeding lust drives away the Spirit and can lead a person to abandon faith.

f.w: looketh upon a woman to lust after her

chapters.n: Adultery is forbidden, and an unrepentant adulterer is to lose Church membership.
Yet full, sincere repentance brings forgiveness, and the Church is commanded to forgive. Repentance here means real change: confessing, forsaking the sin, and not returning to it.
A warning against treating repentance lightly: returning to the same serious sin after being forgiven brings Church discipline.
Saints must not slander their neighbors or harm them in any way. Words can wound as surely as actions.
These moral laws are not new; they are already in the scriptures. The principle holds for all of them: unrepented sin leads to removal from the Church.
The heart of the whole law: love for the Lord shows itself in serving him and keeping all his commandments. This verse bridges the moral laws and the law of consecration that follows.
Here begins the law of consecration. Saints are to remember the poor by dedicating their property to the Lord’s work through a binding legal deed and sacred covenant.

f.g: To dedicate something as sacred, set apart for God’s purposes.

f.w: a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken
f.g: Early Saints signed actual legal deeds transferring property to the bishop.

chapters.n: Giving to the poor is giving to Christ himself. The consecrated property is placed with the bishop and his counselors, who manage it for the Church.

f.w: ye will do it unto me

chapters.n: After consecrating, each person receives back a “stewardship”—property sufficient for his family’s needs. He manages it as a trustee accountable to God rather than as an owner.

f.g: A manager of something that belongs to another; here, the Lord is the true owner.

chapters.n: Any surplus beyond a family’s needs goes to the bishop to help those in want. The goal is that every needy person is “amply supplied.”

f.g: What is left over; the surplus.
“Wants” here means needs, not luxuries (compare D&C 82:17).

chapters.n: The surplus is kept in the Lord’s storehouse—a supply center for the poor—under the direction of Church councils and the bishop.
Storehouse funds also serve broader purposes: buying land for the Church, building meetinghouses, and preparing to build the New Jerusalem.

f.w: the New Jerusalem which is hereafter to be revealed

chapters.n: All of this prepares a gathered, united people for the day the Lord comes to his temple. Consecration has a spiritual aim: the salvation of his people.

f.w: I shall come to my temple

chapters.n: Someone excommunicated for unrepented sin cannot reclaim what he consecrated. What was given to the poor was in fact given to the Lord.
Quoting the Savior’s parable of the sheep and the goats, the Lord explains why: service to the least of his children is service to him.
This fulfills prophecy that converted Gentiles would share their riches with scattered Israel. In the Restoration, Gentile believers help gather and bless the house of Israel.
A second set of instructions begins. Pride is forbidden; dress should be simple, and its beauty should come from honest, homemade work rather than display.

f.w: let all thy garments be plain
f.g: Plain = simple and modest, not showy.

chapters.n: Cleanliness—of body, home, and life—is a commandment. Outward order reflects inward holiness.
Idleness is condemned. Those able to work should not live off the labor of others—an important principle in a system where goods were shared.
The sick who lack faith to be healed but still believe are to be cared for tenderly, with gentle herbal remedies and simple food, and by trustworthy hands rather than enemies.

f.g: Common medical care in 1831; the emphasis is on gentle, careful nursing.

chapters.n: Two or more elders are to pray over the sick and lay hands on them in Christ’s name. Whether the person lives or dies, they belong to the Lord.

f.w: if they die they shall die unto me

chapters.n: The Saints are to love one another so deeply that they mourn when someone dies—especially when that person had no hope of a glorious resurrection. Grief is a sign of love, not of weak faith.

f.w: weep for the loss of them that die

chapters.n: For the faithful, death loses its bitterness. They will not “taste” death in the sense of its terror, for it will be sweet to them.
For those who die without Christ, death is bitter, because they face it without his redemption.

f.g: Woe—sorrow, distress.

chapters.n: Those with faith to be healed will be healed—unless it is their appointed time to die. Healing depends both on faith and on God’s will.
Faith can restore sight, just as Jesus healed the blind.

f.w: He who hath faith to see shall see.

chapters.n: Faith can restore hearing.

f.w: He who hath faith to hear shall hear.

chapters.n: Faith can make the lame leap—language that recalls Isaiah’s prophecy and the healings performed by Jesus and his apostles.
Those who believe but lack faith for healing still may become “sons” of God. The Church is to bear their weaknesses with them as long as they keep God’s laws.
Each person is to faithfully fulfill his own assigned stewardship rather than reach for someone else’s.
Don’t take what belongs to another; pay for what you receive. Even among covenant people who share, honest dealing is required.

f.g: A concrete example meaning any of a fellow member’s possessions.

chapters.n: If a steward gains more than he needs, the surplus goes to the Lord’s storehouse. Consecration is an ongoing practice, not a one-time gift.
Joseph Smith is to keep asking about the scriptures, which will come as the Lord appoints and must be kept safe. This refers to his inspired revision of the Bible.
The new revelations in the Bible translation are not to be taught publicly until the work is complete.

f.g: Keep quiet; do not speak of it.

chapters.n: Once complete, these scriptures are to be taught to everyone in every nation and language.

f.w: all nations, kindreds, tongues and people

chapters.n: The revelations received are to serve as the governing law of the Church. Revealed scripture, not mere custom, directs the Lord’s people.
Obedience brings salvation; persistent disobedience brings damnation—meaning a halt to eternal progress. The phrase “if he so continue” leaves room for repentance.

f.g: Condemned; stopped in progress, unable to receive the full blessings God offers.

chapters.n: A precious promise: those who ask will receive “revelation upon revelation, knowledge upon knowledge.” The mysteries of God are not puzzles but truths that bring peace, joy, and eternal life.

f.g: Truths that can be known only by revelation.

chapters.n: The location of the New Jerusalem will be revealed in the Lord’s timing, as long as the Saints keep asking. It was revealed five months later in Missouri.

f.w: where the New Jerusalem shall be built

chapters.n: Missionaries will be sent in every direction.

f.w: to the east and to the west, to the north and to the south

chapters.n: Converts in the eastern states are to gather west, because of coming troubles and “secret combinations”—conspiracies of evil the Book of Mormon repeatedly warns about.

f.g: Secret alliances bound by oaths to gain power or wealth through wickedness.

chapters.n: Faithful observance brings great reward. The disciples have been given to understand truths that the world, in its unbelief, cannot grasp.

f.w: unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom

chapters.n: A simple charge: keep the laws you have received and stay faithful.
More covenants will come, enough to establish the Saints both in Ohio and in Zion. This looks ahead to later revelations and temple covenants.

f.g: Further commandments and covenants revealed in later sections, such as the law of consecration’s details.

chapters.n: Echoing James 1:5—the very verse that led Joseph Smith to the Sacred Grove—the Lord invites anyone who lacks wisdom to ask, promising generous answers without scolding.

f.w: he that lacketh wisdom, let him ask of me

f.g: Scold or reproach.

chapters.n: The Lord invites the Saints to rejoice, because the keys of the Church—the authority to direct his work—have been given to them.
Priests and teachers, like all members, are to receive stewardships under the law of consecration.
The bishop’s counselors, who give much of their time, may have their families supported from the consecrated property.

f.g: Two elders or high priests assisting the bishop (see v. 31).

chapters.n: Alternatively, they may receive fair compensation for their service, as the bishop and counselors decide.

f.g: Fair payment or compensation.

chapters.n: The bishop, too, may receive support or fair compensation, since his responsibilities would consume much of his time.

Instructions given a couple of weeks later begin here. People who separated from a spouse because that spouse committed sexual sin, and who humbly testify that this is so, are not to be excluded from the Church.

f.g: Divorced or separated from their spouses.

chapters.n: But those who left their spouses in order to commit adultery themselves are to be removed from the Church.
Church leaders are to be careful and look into the circumstances of married people who wish to join, so that such offenders are not received.

f.g: After careful investigation.

chapters.n: Unmarried people seeking membership must repent of all their sins before being received—a requirement of baptism for everyone.
Every member is expected to keep all the commandments and covenants of the Church. Membership is a covenant relationship, not just a label.
Murder is a matter for civil law. The Church does not punish criminals itself; it hands them to the legal authorities, and guilt is to be proved in the courts.
Adultery cases are to be heard by two or more elders, and charges must be established by at least two Church witnesses—not by enemies who may have motives to lie.
If guilt is established by two witnesses, the elders present the case to the Church, which votes by raised hands. Discipline is a careful, public, and orderly process.

f.g: Vote by raising the hand, a practice of common consent (D&C 26:2).

chapters.n: Where possible, the bishop should also be present for such disciplinary hearings.
This orderly procedure is to be used for all such cases.
Robbery is turned over to civil authorities.

f.g: To take by force or threat, as distinct from stealing secretly.

chapters.n: Theft is also turned over to the law of the land.
Lying, where it breaks civil law (such as fraud or false testimony), is likewise handed to the law of the land.
Any other wrongdoing is to be handled according to God’s law—that is, through Church discipline as outlined above.
Personal offenses should first be handled privately and lovingly. If the offender admits the wrong, the two are to be reconciled.

f.w: between him or her and thee alone

chapters.n: If the person won’t admit fault, the matter goes to the elders in a private meeting—not to gossiping members, and not before the world.

f.w: not to the members, but to the elders

chapters.n: A wrong that affects many people is addressed before those affected.
Public sins receive public rebuke, so that the offender feels appropriate shame and turns around. Persistent refusal leads to Church discipline.
Private sins are corrected privately, giving the person a chance to confess quietly to the one wronged and to God, and protecting his or her reputation. The response fits the offense.

f.g: Privately reproved, out of public view.

chapters.n: These principles are to guide the Church in every matter. The law closes as it opened: the Lord’s people are to act in his way.

The Lord calls the elders in Kirtland to listen closely. Some members had been swayed by a woman named Hubble who claimed to receive revelations for the Church, and this revelation answers that confusion.

f.g: Listen carefully.
