chapters.n: The Lord reminds the elders that they already received “a law” for the Church (D&C 42) through the one he appointed—Joseph Smith. Revelation for the whole Church comes through a recognized channel.

f.w: a commandment for a law unto my church

chapters.n: While Joseph remains faithful, no one else is appointed to receive commandments for the Church. The phrase “if he abide in me” makes clear the calling depends on his faithfulness.
Even if Joseph lost this gift, he would still be the one to appoint his successor. The Lord’s house has an orderly line of authority; it cannot be seized by self-proclaimed prophets.

f.g: In his stead = in his place.

chapters.n: As a standing rule, the Saints are not to accept anyone who arrives claiming to bring revelations or commandments for the Church outside this channel.
This rule protects the Saints from deception and gives them a clear test for recognizing teachings that are not from God.

f.w: that you may not be deceived

chapters.n: Those truly called “come in at the gate”—they are properly ordained, as the Lord explained before—and teach the revelations given through the appointed prophet. Compare Jesus’s image of the true shepherd entering by the door.
When the elders meet, they are to teach and strengthen one another so they know how to lead the Church and live its laws. Meetings are for mutual learning, not just listening.

f.g: Build up spiritually.

chapters.n: Learning the Lord’s law is meant to make them holy. They are to commit themselves to act “in all holiness.”

f.g: Made holy, purified and set apart for God.

chapters.n: Faithfulness brings added glory; neglect means losing even what they have. This echoes the Savior’s principle that those who use what they receive are given more.

f.w: it shall be taken, even that which ye have received

chapters.n: The elders must root out sin among them and prepare themselves spiritually before God.

f.g: Clean out completely.

chapters.n: To receive the kingdom’s glories, the Saints are to sustain Joseph Smith and support him through faith-filled prayer. Sustaining a prophet is an active commitment.

f.w: uphold him before me by the prayer of faith

chapters.n: If they want deeper revelation, they should provide Joseph with food, clothing, and what he needs for his work. At this time Joseph had no regular income and was laboring on the Bible translation.

f.g: Clothing.

chapters.n: If they fail to support him, he will stay with those who do receive him. The Lord is gathering a “pure people,” and the blessings follow willing hearts.
Missionaries are not sent out to be taught by the world’s ideas but to teach what the Lord has given them, by the Spirit’s power.

f.w: Ye are not sent forth to be taught, but to teach

chapters.n: They themselves will be taught from heaven. If they sanctify themselves, they will be “endowed with power”—a promise later tied to the Kirtland Temple.
The “great day of the Lord”—his Second Coming—is near, so this is no time for distraction.

f.w: the great day of the Lord is nigh

chapters.n: A dramatic picture of the Lord’s coming: heaven and earth shake and a trumpet calls the righteous dead to rise, while the wicked dead must wait for a later resurrection.

f.w: ye sinners stay and sleep until I shall call again

chapters.n: Therefore, prepare for action and holiness, so you are not counted among the wicked when that day comes.

f.g: Literally, tuck up long robes for work or travel; figuratively, get ready.

chapters.n: Elders are to raise their voices boldly and warn everyone—young and old, enslaved and free—to prepare for the Lord’s coming.

f.g: Hold nothing back.
Enslaved and free people.

chapters.n: If people reject the Lord when he calls through mortal messengers, how will they respond when nature itself thunders the same message? Warnings will grow louder if ignored.

f.w: if I, who am a man
f.g: The Lord here speaks of calling through his human servants, or of himself as one who once lived as a man.

chapters.n: Lightning flashing from east to west will join the call to repent. In scripture, signs in nature often function as God’s voice.

f.w: the lightnings shall streak forth from the east unto the west

chapters.n: Finally, the Lord himself will speak from heaven to all nations, reminding them that he is their Creator.
Using Jesus’s tender image from his lament over Jerusalem, the Lord mourns that he has often tried to gather the nations to safety, but they refused.

f.w: as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings

chapters.n: A sweeping list of the ways God calls his children: prophets, angels, his own voice, natural disasters, judgments, mercy, and the promise of eternal life. Every voice has the same purpose—to save—but many still refuse.

f.w: by the voice of judgment, and by the voice of mercy

f.g: Deadly epidemic diseases.

chapters.n: The cup of God’s anger is full—the time of judgment has come for the persistently wicked. A “cup” is a biblical image for one’s allotted portion.

f.w: the cup of the wrath of mine indignation

chapters.n: The Lord seals his message: these are his own words.
This is the final call to work in the Lord’s vineyard—the world—before he comes. Compare the Book of Mormon’s allegory of the olive tree, where the servants labor one last time.

f.w: labor ye in my vineyard for the last time

chapters.n: In his own timing the Lord will come in judgment, and his redeemed people will reign with him on the earth.

f.w: shall reign with me on earth

chapters.n: The Millennium—a thousand years of peace foretold by prophets—will surely come.

f.g: Latin for “thousand years”; the period of Christ’s personal reign on earth.

chapters.n: Satan will be bound during the Millennium. Afterward he will be released briefly before the final end of the earth as we know it.
The righteous living at that time will be changed to immortality instantly, and the earth will be transformed as if by fire.

f.w: changed in the twinkling of an eye

chapters.n: The fate of the wicked is described as unquenchable fire, but its full nature is not revealed to mortals; it will be known at the judgment.
Jesus Christ names himself and asks the elders to treasure these words and let the seriousness of eternity weigh on their minds.

f.w: Treasure these things up in your hearts

f.g: The weighty, serious realities of eternal life and judgment.

chapters.n: A brief closing charge: be serious-minded and keep every commandment.

f.g: Be clear-headed, earnest, and self-controlled.

chapters.n: The Lord tells Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to call the elders together from every direction, by letter or other means. This led to a Church conference held in Kirtland in June 1831.

f.g: Wise, fitting, or needed.

chapters.n: If the elders come faithfully and with faith, the Lord promises to pour out his Spirit on them during the gathering.

f.w: I will pour out my Spirit

chapters.n: From the conference the elders will go into the surrounding areas to preach repentance.
Many will join the Church, giving the Saints enough strength to organize legally under the laws of the land.

f.w: according to the laws of man
f.g: Through legal organization the Church could hold property and protect its rights.

chapters.n: Legal organization would protect the Saints from enemies, help them keep God’s laws, and break the snares of those who want to destroy them.

f.g: Every chain or restraint.

chapters.n: The Saints must care for the poor and needy until the law of consecration can be fully put in place. Caring for the poor is never postponed.

f.w: visit the poor and the needy

chapters.n: Speaking amid false rumors about the Church, the Lord introduces himself as the Creator of heaven and earth. The One who made all things is the One now speaking to his people.

f.w: by whom all things were made
live, and move, and have a being

chapters.n: Listen now, the Lord urges, before death comes unexpectedly. Jeremiah’s lament—“the harvest is past, the summer is ended”—warns against putting off repentance.

f.w: the summer shall be past, and the harvest ended

chapters.n: Christ describes himself as our “advocate”—like a defense lawyer pleading our case before the Father.
Christ’s plea rests not on our merits but on his own: he points to his sinless life, his suffering, and his shed blood, which the Father gave so that the Father might be glorified.

f.w: in whom thou wast well pleased

chapters.n: The Savior asks the Father to spare those who believe in him so they can come to him and receive eternal life. This is the heart of Christ’s intercession.
Listen while it is still “today”—while there is time—and don’t harden your hearts. The phrase echoes Psalm 95, quoted in Hebrews.
Christ declares he is Alpha and Omega—the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet—the beginning and the end. He is the light of the world, shining even where darkness fails to understand it.
Echoing John’s Gospel, Christ recalls that his own people rejected him in mortality, yet those who received him gained power to become God’s children and inherit eternal life.

f.w: I came unto mine own, and mine own received me not

chapters.n: The restored gospel—his “everlasting covenant”—is sent into the world as a light, a rallying flag, and a forerunner preparing the way for his return.

f.g: A banner or flag around which people rally.

chapters.n: Christ invites people to come and reason with him, as he did with prophets of old. Faith is not blind; the Lord offers “strong reasoning.”
He offers the wisdom of the God of Enoch—the ancient prophet whose story is told more fully in the book of Moses.

Enoch and his people were so righteous that their city was taken from the earth to God. It is “reserved” until a day of righteousness; holy men in later ages sought such a society but could not find it because of wickedness.

f.w: a city reserved until a day of righteousness shall come

chapters.n: These seekers confessed they were strangers and pilgrims—travelers whose true home was not this fallen world.
Yet they were promised that they would one day see that righteous city—in resurrected bodies.
The Lord prepares to prophesy plainly, as he did to people in ancient times.
He now retells, with added clarity, what he taught his apostles on the Mount of Olives about the signs of his coming. This is often called the Olivet Discourse.

f.w: concerning the signs of my coming

chapters.n: A unique detail: the ancient righteous felt the separation of spirit from body as a kind of bondage. The Lord explains how resurrection—“the day of redemption”—and the gathering of Israel will come.

f.w: the restoration of the scattered Israel

chapters.n: Speaking to his disciples beside Herod’s temple in Jerusalem, Jesus notes that enemies of the Jews think the temple could never fall.

f.w: this temple which is in Jerusalem

chapters.n: Destruction will come suddenly on that generation, and the Jewish people will be scattered among the nations. This was fulfilled when the Romans destroyed Jerusalem in AD 70.

f.w: as a thief in the night

chapters.n: The temple will be utterly demolished—not one stone left on another. The Romans burned and dismantled it.

f.w: there shall not be left one stone upon another

chapters.n: The prophecies about Jerusalem’s fall would happen within the lifetime of that very generation.

f.w: this generation of Jews shall not pass away

chapters.n: The disciples know the world will end and heaven and earth will pass away.
Jesus affirms they are right, but stresses that his words will be fulfilled before that end comes.

f.w: these things which I have told you shall not pass away

chapters.n: After Jerusalem’s fall, a remnant of the Jews will be scattered among all nations.

f.g: A surviving portion of a people.

chapters.n: They will be gathered again, but only after the “times of the Gentiles” are fulfilled—a period when the gospel goes primarily to non-Israelite nations.

f.w: the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled

chapters.n: In that era there will be wars and rumors of wars, worldwide turmoil, and fear. Many will claim Christ’s coming is far off—a scoffing attitude Peter also foretold.
Love will grow cold and wickedness will spread.

f.w: the love of men shall wax cold

f.g: Grow or become.

chapters.n: When the times of the Gentiles arrive, a light will break out among people in spiritual darkness: the fulness of the gospel—understood by Latter-day Saints as the Restoration.

f.w: a light shall break forth among them that sit in darkness

chapters.n: But many Gentiles will not receive it. Following human philosophies and traditions, they will fail to recognize the light.
In the generation when the fulness of the gospel is offered and rejected, the times of the Gentiles will be fulfilled, and the gospel will turn again to Israel.

f.w: in that generation shall the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled

chapters.n: Some living in that generation will witness an “overflowing scourge”—a devastating, spreading sickness.
Disciples will stand firm in holy places, while some of the wicked will curse God even as they suffer. Holy places include temples, homes, and lives centered on God.
Earthquakes and disasters will come, yet many will still harden their hearts and turn to violence against one another.

f.g: Various, many different.

chapters.n: The disciples were troubled by these grim prophecies.
Jesus comforts them: when these things happen, they can know his promises are being fulfilled. The signs are meant to reassure the faithful, not terrify them.
When the gospel light begins to break forth, it will be like a parable he is about to give.
The parable of the fig tree: when tender leaves appear, people know summer is near.
So when the faithful see these signs, they will know the Lord’s coming is close.
Those who revere God will watch eagerly for the signs of his coming. Watching is an expression of faith.

f.g: Fear here means reverent awe and respect.

chapters.n: Signs will appear in the heavens and on the earth.
Blood, fire, and columns of smoke will be seen—images drawn from Joel’s prophecy.

f.w: blood, and fire, and vapors of smoke

chapters.n: Before the great day, the sun will darken, the moon appear blood-red, and stars fall from the sky.

f.w: the sun shall be darkened, and the moon be turned into blood

chapters.n: The remnant of the Jews will be gathered to Jerusalem.

f.g: Jerusalem, where Jesus was speaking.

chapters.n: Then they will look for the Messiah, and he will come in the clouds with power, glory, and his holy angels. Those who do not watch will be cut off.

f.w: clothed with power and great glory

chapters.n: Before judgment falls, an angel will sound a trumpet and the righteous dead will rise to meet the Lord.

f.w: the saints that have slept shall come forth to meet me in the cloud

f.g: A biblical image of God’s power in action.

chapters.n: Those who died in peace are blessed. Just as the disciples now see Christ, they too will come to him and their redemption will be complete as Saints rise from every part of the earth.

f.w: the four quarters of the earth
f.g: The four directions—everywhere on earth.

chapters.n: Then the Lord’s power will fall upon the wicked nations.
The Lord will stand on the Mount of Olives, which will split in two, as the earth trembles—a prophecy from Zechariah.

f.w: set his foot upon this mount, and it shall cleave in twain

f.g: Split in two.

chapters.n: The Lord’s voice will be heard everywhere. Nations will mourn, and those who mocked will realize their folly.

f.w: the nations of the earth shall mourn

chapters.n: Mockers and scorners will meet calamity, and those who looked for chances to do evil will be cut down.

f.w: they that have watched for iniquity

chapters.n: Then the Jews will see the Lord and ask about the wounds in his hands and feet—a moving prophecy from Zechariah of recognition at last.

f.w: What are these wounds in thine hands

chapters.n: Jesus will identify himself plainly: he was wounded “in the house of my friends,” crucified, and is the Son of God. Their long-awaited Messiah is the one their ancestors rejected.

f.w: I am Jesus that was crucified

chapters.n: They will weep for their sins and mourn that they persecuted their king.
Nations who never had God’s law will be redeemed and share in the first resurrection; their judgment will be bearable. God is fair to those who never had a chance to know him.

f.g: Peoples who did not know the God of Israel.

chapters.n: Satan will be bound so that he has no place in people’s hearts—partly because the righteous will no longer give him room.
When Christ comes in glory, his parable of the ten virgins will be fulfilled.
Here the Lord explains the parable: the wise virgins are those who have received the truth, taken the Holy Spirit as their guide, and not been deceived. They will endure the day of his coming.

f.w: have taken the Holy Spirit for their guide

chapters.n: The earth will be given to the righteous as an inheritance, and their children will grow up without sin unto salvation during the Millennium.

f.w: the earth shall be given unto them for an inheritance
their children shall grow up without sin

chapters.n: The Lord will dwell among them as their king and lawgiver.
Turning to Joseph Smith, the Lord says no more will be revealed on this chapter (Matthew 24) until the New Testament is translated. The expanded version appears in Joseph Smith—Matthew.

f.w: until the New Testament be translated
f.g: Joseph had been revising the Old Testament; here he is told to begin the New Testament.

chapters.n: Therefore Joseph is commanded to start translating the New Testament now, to prepare the Saints for coming events.
Great things lie ahead for the Saints.
Wars abroad will soon come close to home; within a few years they will hear of wars in their own lands—fulfilled in part by later conflicts including the American Civil War.
So the elders are to gather from the eastern states, go west preaching repentance, and establish branches where people repent.

f.w: gather ye out from the eastern lands

chapters.n: United in heart and purpose, the Saints are to pool their means to purchase an inheritance the Lord will appoint later.

f.w: with one heart and with one mind

chapters.n: This land will be the New Jerusalem: a place of peace, refuge, and safety for the Saints.

f.g: An echo of the Old Testament cities of refuge where people could find protection.

chapters.n: God’s glory will rest there, and his power will be so evident that the wicked will stay away. It will be called Zion.
In a violent world, anyone who refuses to fight his neighbor will need to flee to Zion for safety.
People from every nation will gather to Zion, the only people not at war with one another.

f.w: out of every nation under heaven

chapters.n: The wicked will say among themselves that Zion’s people are too formidable to attack. Here “terrible” means awe-inspiring, not cruel.

f.g: Inspiring awe or fear—because of God’s power with them.

chapters.n: The righteous will come to Zion from every nation, singing songs of everlasting joy.

f.w: singing with songs of everlasting joy

chapters.n: For now, the Saints should keep these plans private until the Lord’s timing is right, so their enemies don’t interfere before the work is done.

f.w: keep these things from going abroad
f.g: Don’t spread them widely yet.

chapters.n: When the world does learn of it, they may then consider these things seriously.
When the Lord appears, he will be fearsome to the wicked; they will stand far off and tremble.
All nations will fear the Lord’s power. The revelation closes as it began, with the majesty of the Creator.
The Lord speaks to the Saints in Kirtland, where questions had arisen about who could attend Church meetings. What he has revealed is meant to help them and teach them.

f.g: Benefit, spiritual gain.

chapters.n: Despite any written rules, elders have always been meant to lead meetings as the Holy Spirit directs. Meetings are to be Spirit-led, not run by rigid formula.

f.w: as they are directed and guided by the Holy Spirit

chapters.n: Public meetings must be open to everyone; no one is to be turned away. Some early members had wanted to exclude non-members.
Church members are not to be excluded from sacrament meetings either, though anyone who has sinned should refrain from partaking of the sacrament until they have made things right.

f.w: let him not partake until he makes reconciliation

chapters.n: Sincere seekers who are not members are also welcome in sacrament meetings. The Lord wants seekers to feel the Spirit among his people.
The same applies to confirmation meetings, where new members received the gift of the Holy Ghost: earnest seekers may stay.

f.g: Meetings where newly baptized members were confirmed and received the gift of the Holy Ghost.

chapters.n: In all things the Saints should ask God, who gives generously, and follow what the Spirit confirms—living uprightly, praying, and giving thanks. This guards against teachings that come from evil spirits or from merely human ideas.

f.w: ask of God, who giveth liberally

chapters.n: To avoid deception, seek earnestly the best spiritual gifts, always remembering their purpose. Spiritual gifts are protection as well as blessing.

f.w: seek ye earnestly the best gifts

chapters.n: Spiritual gifts are given to bless those who love God and keep his commandments—and those trying to. They are not for showing off or seeking signs to satisfy selfish desires.

f.w: him that seeketh so to do
f.g: A gracious clause: gifts are offered to those still striving, not only to the already perfect.

chapters.n: The Saints are asked to keep in mind the list of gifts that follows, so they can recognize genuine gifts of the Spirit.
No one has every gift, but everyone has at least one. This is a great equalizer: every member has something spiritual to contribute.

f.w: to every man is given a gift by the Spirit of God

chapters.n: Gifts are spread among people so that all can benefit from one another. The Church needs each person’s gift, much as a body needs every part.

f.w: that all may be profited thereby

chapters.n: The first gift listed: a sure witness by the Holy Ghost that Jesus is the Son of God, crucified for the world’s sins. This is the gift of testimony.

f.w: to know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God

chapters.n: A companion gift: to believe the testimony of others. Those who trust another’s witness can also gain eternal life if they stay faithful—a comforting truth for those still growing in testimony.
Some are given understanding of the different ways the Lord administers his Church—how his work is organized and led, adapted mercifully to people’s circumstances.
Some can discern the “diversities of operations”—that is, whether various spiritual influences are from God. Every member should benefit from true spiritual manifestations.

f.g: To benefit from it.

chapters.n: Some receive the gift of wisdom: knowing how to apply truth well in life.

f.g: Here, a spiritual gift of wise counsel—not the health code later revealed in D&C 89.

chapters.n: Others receive the gift of knowledge, so they can teach others to become wise and knowledgeable.
Some have faith to be healed.
Others have faith to heal others.
Some are given power to work miracles.
Others are given the gift of prophecy—speaking by inspiration, often bearing witness of Christ.
Others can discern spirits—recognizing whether an influence comes from God or not. This was badly needed in Kirtland at the time.
Some can speak in tongues—languages they have not learned—by the Spirit, often to share the gospel.
Others can interpret tongues, so the gift edifies those who hear.
Every one of these gifts comes from God and is meant to bless his children.

f.w: all these gifts come from God

chapters.n: Bishops and other appointed leaders are given the gift of discerning all these gifts, so they can detect counterfeits among those claiming spiritual power.
Whoever asks in the Spirit will receive in the Spirit.
Some leaders may receive all the gifts so the Church has a head that can bless every member.

f.g: Presiding leadership, such as the President of the Church.

chapters.n: When a person prays under the Spirit’s guidance, he asks for what God wants, so the prayer is granted.

f.w: asketh according to the will of God

chapters.n: Whatever is done by the Spirit should be done in Christ’s name.

f.w: all things must be done in the name of Christ

chapters.n: The Saints must thank God in the Spirit for every blessing.
Finally, they must continually live virtuous and holy lives. Gifts of the Spirit flourish where virtue is practiced.
John Whitmer is asked to write a regular history of the Church and help Joseph Smith copy the revelations. John had been helping as a scribe; history-keeping was now formally his assignment.

f.g: John Whitmer, an older brother of David Whitmer and one of the Eight Witnesses of the Book of Mormon.

chapters.n: John may also speak in Church meetings when appropriate. His calling is not only to record but to teach.
He is appointed to keep the Church’s records and history continually, because Oliver Cowdery, the first recorder, has been called to other work.

f.w: Oliver Cowdery I have appointed to another office
f.g: Oliver had gone on a mission to the Lamanites on Missouri’s western frontier.

chapters.n: John was reluctant to accept, but the Lord promises that if he is faithful, the Comforter will help him write. Inspired help comes even for record-keeping.
For now, the Ohio Saints should stay where they are living, as suits their situations. They had asked whether to prepare for an immediate move.

f.g: Homes, where they live.

chapters.n: Those who own land are to share with the Saints arriving from New York and other eastern places.
Those without land should buy property nearby for the time being, since the incoming Saints need somewhere to live.
The Saints must save money and earn honestly so that in time they can buy land for the promised city, Zion. Righteous preparation is part of building Zion.

f.w: obtain all that ye can in righteousness

f.g: The New Jerusalem, whose location would be revealed in Missouri later in 1831.

chapters.n: The place of the city has not yet been revealed. After the eastern Saints arrive, men will be appointed to whom the location will be made known.
These men will purchase lands and lay the city’s foundation. Then families will gather in order, as directed by the presidency and bishop, according to the Lord’s laws.
The Lord sends Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, and Leman Copley to preach to the Shakers near Cleveland, Ohio. They are to teach the gospel just as they received it, not watered down.

f.g: The United Society of Believers in Christ’s Second Appearing, a celibate communal group named for the shaking in their worship.
Leman Copley, a recent convert who had formerly been a Shaker.

chapters.n: The Shakers want part of the truth, but not all of it. They are not right before the Lord and need to repent.
Sidney and Parley, experienced preachers, are the main messengers.
Leman is to be ordained and reason with the Shakers, but only on the basis of what Sidney and Parley teach him—not his old Shaker beliefs. Obedience would bring blessing.

f.w: not according to that which he has received of them
f.g: Leman still held some Shaker ideas; he is told to set them aside.

chapters.n: God the Father speaks of sending his Only Begotten Son to redeem the world. Salvation depends on receiving Christ.

People treated the Son of Man as they pleased, even crucifying him; yet he now reigns in heaven and will descend to put all enemies under his feet. The Shakers believed Christ had already returned—this verse says he has not yet.

f.g: Listed = wished, pleased.

f.w: put all enemies under his feet

chapters.n: No one—not even the angels—knows the day and hour of his coming. This directly answered Shaker claims that the Second Coming had already happened.

f.w: the hour and the day no man knoweth

chapters.n: All people need repentance, for all are under sin—except holy men the Lord has reserved, unknown to the elders. Latter-day Saints often understand these to include translated beings.

f.w: holy men that ye know not of

chapters.n: The Lord has restored his everlasting covenant—the gospel that has existed from the beginning.
God fulfills his promises. The nations will bow to this covenant; those that exalt themselves will be humbled by his power.

f.w: that which is now exalted of itself shall be laid low

chapters.n: The missionaries are to preach as Peter did on the day of Pentecost.

f.w: mine apostle of old, whose name was Peter

chapters.n: First, believe in Jesus, who lived on earth and is yet to come—the beginning and the end.

f.g: Emphasizes his Second Coming is still future, contrary to Shaker belief.

chapters.n: Then repent and be baptized in Christ’s name for the forgiveness of sins—as Peter taught. The Shakers did not practice baptism.

f.g: Forgiveness, release.

chapters.n: Those who do will receive the gift of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by elders.

f.w: by the laying on of the hands

chapters.n: Anyone who forbids marriage is not sent by God, because marriage is God’s institution. The Shakers required celibacy.
It is right for a man to have a wife, and the two become one flesh, so the earth may fulfill the purpose of its creation.

f.w: they twain shall be one flesh

f.g: Two.

chapters.n: Marriage and family allow the earth to be filled with the number of God’s spirit children planned before the world was made.

f.g: The full number of human beings God intended to send to earth.

chapters.n: Anyone who commands people to abstain from meat is not sent by God. Some Shakers avoided pork or meat.
Animals, birds, and plants are provided for human food and clothing, in abundance.

f.w: is ordained for the use of man

chapters.n: Yet no one should possess more than another—inequality is part of why the world lies in sin. This echoes the law of consecration.

f.w: not given that one man should possess that which is above another

chapters.n: Woe to anyone who kills animals or wastes meat without need. God’s gifts are not to be squandered.

f.w: wasteth flesh and hath no need

chapters.n: The Son of Man will not come as a woman, nor as a man walking about on earth. The Shakers believed Christ’s second appearing had come through their founder, Ann Lee.

f.g: A direct correction of the Shaker teaching about Ann Lee.

f.w: neither of a man traveling on the earth

chapters.n: Don’t be deceived; stay steady and watch for his true coming, when heaven shakes, the earth reels like a drunkard, valleys rise, and mountains fall—all at the angel’s trumpet.

f.w: reel to and fro as a drunken man
for the valleys to be exalted

chapters.n: Before that great day, Jacob (Israel) will flourish in the wilderness and the Lamanites will blossom like a rose.

f.w: the Lamanites shall blossom as the rose

chapters.n: Zion will flourish on the hills and mountains and be gathered to the place the Lord has appointed.

f.w: Zion shall flourish upon the hills

chapters.n: The missionaries are to go, repent of their own sins, and ask and knock in prayer.

f.w: ask and ye shall receive; knock and it shall be opened unto you

chapters.n: The Lord will go ahead of them and guard them from behind, and be among them. They will not be confused or defeated.

f.g: Rearguard—protection from behind.
Put to shame or thrown into confusion.

chapters.n: Jesus Christ signs the revelation, declaring that he comes quickly. (The Shakers largely rejected the elders’ message.)

The living God calls the elders to listen. In early 1831 some Ohio converts were showing wild behavior—fainting, contortions, strange “visions”—claiming it was spiritual. The elders had asked the Lord about these spirits.

f.w: the spirits which have gone abroad in the earth
f.g: Spiritual influences and manifestations circulating among people, some of them false.

chapters.n: Many false spirits are at work in the world, deceiving people.
Satan has been trying to deceive the Saints themselves in order to overthrow them.

f.w: Satan hath sought to deceive you

chapters.n: The Lord has seen abominations—serious wrongs—in the church that claims his name.

f.g: Things that are deeply offensive to God.

chapters.n: Those who remain faithful and endure, whether they live or die, will inherit eternal life.
Woe to deceivers and hypocrites—the Lord will bring them to judgment.

f.g: People who pretend to be what they are not.

chapters.n: Some hypocrites in the Church have misled others, giving the adversary power. But those who were misled can be reclaimed—brought back.

f.g: Rescued and brought back.

chapters.n: The hypocrites will be exposed and cut off from the Church in God’s timing. Those cut off have been overcome by the world.
Therefore everyone should be careful not to act in ways that are untrue or unrighteous before God.
The Lord invites the elders to “reason together” so they can understand—God engages their minds, not just their emotions.
He will reason with them as one person speaks to another, face to face.
Just as people understand each other when they speak plainly, the Lord will speak in a way they can grasp. God adapts his teaching to human understanding.
The Lord asks a direct question: what were you ordained to do?
The answer: to preach his gospel by the Spirit—the Comforter sent to teach truth.

f.w: the Comforter which was sent forth to teach the truth

chapters.n: Yet they accepted spirits they couldn’t understand and assumed they were from God. Were they justified in that? The Lord asks them to think it through.

f.g: Here, “in the right” or approved.

chapters.n: They must answer for themselves, but the Lord promises mercy: those who are weak will be made strong.

f.w: he that is weak among you hereafter shall be made strong

chapters.n: A teacher sent to preach truth by the Comforter—does he do it by the Spirit of truth, or some other way?
If by any other way, it is not of God. Charisma, cleverness, or excitement cannot replace the Spirit.
Likewise, does the listener receive the word by the Spirit of truth, or another way?
If another way, it is not of God. Both teacher and learner need the Spirit.
Why can’t they see it? When a person receives the word by the Spirit, he receives it just as it was taught by the Spirit.
So teacher and learner understand each other, are both built up, and rejoice together. This is a key pattern for gospel teaching.

f.w: both are edified and rejoice together

chapters.n: Whatever doesn’t edify—build people up spiritually—is not of God; it is darkness. A clear test for any spiritual experience.

f.w: that which doth not edify is not of God

f.g: Build up, strengthen, enlighten.

chapters.n: What comes from God is light. Those who receive light and stay faithful receive more, and it grows brighter until “the perfect day.” Spiritual growth is gradual and progressive.

f.w: groweth brighter and brighter until the perfect day

chapters.n: The Lord teaches these truths so the elders can drive darkness out from among them.
The one ordained and sent by God is appointed to be greatest—yet he is the least and the servant of all. True greatness is service.
Such a servant is, in a sense, “possessor of all things,” because heaven’s power and light are available to him through the Father and the Son.
But no one possesses all things unless he is cleansed from all sin. Purity is the condition for this power.
Those who are cleansed may ask whatever they will in Jesus’s name and it will be done.

f.w: ask whatsoever you will in the name of Jesus

chapters.n: The Spirit will tell them what to ask for. As leaders, they will have power over spirits.

f.w: it shall be given you what you shall ask

chapters.n: A practical test: if they see a spiritual manifestation they cannot understand or receive, they should pray to the Father in Jesus’s name. If the Father does not give them that spirit, they will know it is not of God.

f.w: ye shall ask of the Father in the name of Jesus

chapters.n: They will then have power over that spirit and may declare loudly that it is not of God.
But not with insults or boasting—otherwise they themselves might be overcome. Even rebuking evil must be done humbly.

f.g: Abusive, insulting language.

chapters.n: Whoever receives something from God should recognize it as God’s gift and rejoice that God counted him worthy.
By heeding what they have received and will receive, they will be given the kingdom and power to overcome everything not ordained by God.
Those hearing these words from Joseph Smith are told their sins are forgiven—a tender reassurance after correction.
Joseph Wakefield and Parley P. Pratt are to visit the branches and strengthen them through encouragement.

f.g: Urgent encouragement.

chapters.n: John Corrill and other ordained men should do the same work, and no one should stop them.
Bishop Edward Partridge was wrong in this matter, apparently in some way hindering these assignments, but if he repents he will be forgiven.
The Lord calls them little children who can’t bear everything yet; they must grow in grace and knowledge.

f.w: grow in grace and in the knowledge of the truth

chapters.n: Do not fear—you are mine, and I have overcome the world. They belong to the group the Father gave to Christ.

f.w: that my Father hath given me

chapters.n: None whom the Father has given him will be lost.
The Father and the Son are one in purpose. Those who receive Christ are in him, and he in them.

f.w: I am in the Father and the Father in me

chapters.n: Christ is among them as the Good Shepherd and the Stone of Israel. Whoever builds on this rock will never fall.

f.w: He that buildeth upon this rock

chapters.n: A day will come when they will hear his voice, see him, and know that he is.

f.w: see me, and know that I am

chapters.n: Therefore watch, so you are ready.
The Lord gives Bishop Edward Partridge instructions on organizing the Saints from Colesville, New York, who had just arrived in Thompson, Ohio.

f.g: The Colesville Branch, recently gathered from New York.

chapters.n: They must be organized by the Lord’s laws—meaning the law of consecration—or they will be cut off.
Bishop Partridge and his chosen helpers are to give each family a portion, equal according to family size, circumstances, and needs. Equality here is fairness, not identical shares.

f.w: every man equal according to his family

chapters.n: Each person receives a written deed securing his portion as a right in the Church, held as long as he remains a member in good standing.

f.g: A legal deed.

chapters.n: If someone leaves the Church through transgression, he cannot reclaim what he consecrated for the poor, but he keeps the portion deeded to him. This later provision protected both the Church and individuals.

f.w: that portion that is deeded unto him

chapters.n: Everything should be secured according to the laws of the land—legal and orderly.

f.w: according to the laws of the land

chapters.n: What belongs to these Saints should be assigned to them.
An agent should be appointed to manage the group’s remaining money and buy food and clothing as needed.

f.g: A business representative for the community.

chapters.n: Everyone must deal honestly and be equal, receiving alike, so that they may be one as the Lord commanded.
Property belonging to this community should not be transferred to another branch.

f.g: Another local congregation or branch of the Church.

chapters.n: If another branch wants money from this one, they should repay it by agreement.
Such transactions go through the bishop or the agent chosen by the members.

f.w: by the voice of the church
f.g: By common consent of the members.

chapters.n: The bishop is to establish a storehouse, where surplus money and food beyond the people’s needs are kept.

f.g: Food in general, not just animal flesh.

chapters.n: The bishop may also keep what he and his family need while he is occupied with this work.
This is granted as a privilege: the opportunity to live by God’s laws.
The Lord consecrates the Thompson land to them for a short time, until he directs them elsewhere. (They soon moved to Missouri; see D&C 54.)
Since they don’t know how long they will stay, they should act as though they will be there for years. Working as if staying long brings good results.
This arrangement serves as a model for Bishop Partridge in other branches.

f.g: A pattern or template.

chapters.n: Faithful, just, and wise stewards will enter into their Lord’s joy and inherit eternal life.

f.w: enter into the joy of his Lord

chapters.n: Jesus Christ declares he comes quickly, at an unexpected hour.

f.w: in an hour you think not

chapters.n: The Lord speaks to the elders after a June 1831 conference in Kirtland, where the first high priests had been ordained.
He outlines what they should do until the next conference, to be held in Missouri, the land to be consecrated for his people—a remnant of Jacob and heirs of the covenant.
Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to travel to Missouri as soon as they can prepare.
If faithful, they will learn what to do.
And if faithful, they will be shown the land of the Saints’ inheritance. This was fulfilled in D&C 57.
If unfaithful, they will be cut off as the Lord sees fit. Even Joseph and Sidney are not exempt from conditions.
Lyman Wight and John Corrill are to travel quickly.
John Murdock and Hyrum Smith, the Prophet’s older brother, are to go by way of Detroit.

f.g: Then a small city in Michigan Territory.

chapters.n: They are to preach along the way, teaching only what prophets and apostles have written and what the Comforter teaches them.

f.w: saying none other things than that which the prophets and apostles have written

chapters.n: They go two by two, preaching in every congregation, baptizing and confirming right at the water’s edge.

f.w: the laying on of the hands by the water's side
f.g: Confirmation performed immediately after baptism.

chapters.n: The Lord will cut his work short in righteousness—he will hasten it—for judgment is coming, leading to victory.

f.w: cut my work short in righteousness

chapters.n: Lyman Wight is warned that Satan wants to sift him like chaff—to separate him from the faithful.

f.g: The light husks blown away when grain is winnowed.

chapters.n: The faithful will be made rulers over many things.
The Lord gives a pattern for recognizing truth, since Satan is deceiving the nations.
Part one: a person who prays with a contrite spirit and obeys the ordinances is accepted by God.

f.g: Humble, repentant, and teachable.

chapters.n: Part two: a speaker with a contrite spirit, meek language, and edifying words is of God, if he obeys the ordinances.

f.g: Gentle, humble, not arrogant.

chapters.n: Part three: one who trembles under God’s power will be made strong and produce praise and wisdom consistent with revelation.

f.w: he that trembleth under my power

chapters.n: Whoever is overcome and doesn’t produce such fruits is not of the Lord.
By this pattern, they can discern spirits anywhere.
The time has come: it will be done to people according to their faith.

f.w: according to men's faith it shall be done unto them

chapters.n: This applies to all the elders he has chosen.
Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre are to preach on the way to Missouri. (Ezra later delayed, and his call was reassigned in D&C 56.)
Isaac Morley and Ezra Booth are also assigned. Booth later became disillusioned and wrote published letters attacking the Church.
Edward Partridge and Martin Harris are to travel with Sidney and Joseph.
David Whitmer—one of the Three Witnesses—and Harvey Whitlock are to go and preach.
The brothers Parley P. Pratt and Orson Pratt are to go and preach.
Solomon Hancock and Simeon Carter are assigned.
Edson Fuller and Jacob Scott are assigned.
Levi W. Hancock and Zebedee Coltrin are assigned. Both would later serve in Church leadership in Kirtland.
Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith, Joseph’s younger brother, are assigned.

f.g: One of the Eight Witnesses and an early missionary.

chapters.n: Wheeler Baldwin and William Carter are assigned.
Newel Knight and Selah J. Griffin are to be ordained and travel together.
All are to go to one place by different routes, without building on another’s work or following another’s path—spreading the message as widely as possible.

f.w: one man shall not build upon another's foundation

chapters.n: The faithful will be preserved and blessed with much fruit—converts and growth.
Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey are sent east instead.
They may work among their families, declaring only what prophets and apostles taught and what they have personally witnessed and believe.

f.w: that which they have seen and heard

chapters.n: Because of transgression, Heman Basset’s calling is taken and given to Simonds Ryder. (Ryder later left the Church and joined the mob that attacked Joseph Smith in Hiram in 1832.)

f.g: An early member involved in the strange spiritual manifestations in Kirtland.

chapters.n: Jared Carter and George James are to be ordained priests.
The remaining elders are to watch over the branches, preach nearby, and support themselves by their own labor, guarding against idolatry and wickedness.
In everything, remember the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted—those who don’t are not Christ’s disciples. Discipleship is measured by compassion.

f.w: the same is not my disciple

chapters.n: Joseph, Sidney, and Edward Partridge are to carry a letter of recommendation from the Church, and one should be prepared for Oliver Cowdery, already in Missouri.

f.g: A certificate showing standing in the Church.

chapters.n: If faithful, they will gather to rejoice in Missouri, their land of inheritance, which at present belongs to their enemies.
The Lord will hasten the city of Zion in his own time and crown the faithful with joy.
Jesus Christ, the Son of God, promises to lift the faithful up at the last day.

f.w: I will lift them up at the last day

chapters.n: Algernon Sidney Gilbert, a Kirtland merchant and business partner of Newel K. Whitney, had prayed to know his place in the restored Church. The Lord tells him his prayers are heard.

f.g: Algernon Sidney Gilbert (1789–1834), who later ran the Church store in Independence, Missouri.
Here, his assignment and role in the Church.

chapters.n: The Savior, identifying himself as the one crucified for the world’s sins, asks Sidney to forsake the world—to put worldly pursuits second to God’s work.
He is to be ordained an elder to preach faith, repentance, forgiveness of sins, and the gift of the Holy Ghost—the first principles and ordinances of the gospel.

f.w: faith and repentance and remission of sins

chapters.n: He will also be an agent for the Church, handling business affairs where the bishop directs. His business skills are put to sacred use.
He is to travel to Missouri with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon.
These are his first assignments; more will come according to his faithful labor. Callings unfold over time.

f.g: The remainder.

chapters.n: Finally: only those who endure to the end are saved. Gilbert served faithfully until he died of cholera in Missouri in 1834.

f.w: he only is saved who endureth unto the end

chapters.n: The Lord introduces himself as Alpha and Omega and as the crucified Redeemer, speaking to the troubled Colesville Saints in Thompson, Ohio.
Newel Knight, the branch leader, is told to stand firm in his calling despite the turmoil.

f.g: Leader of the Colesville Saints; his healing from an evil influence in 1830 was among the Church’s first recorded miracles.

chapters.n: If the Saints want to escape their enemies, they must repent fully and become humble and contrite.

f.g: Sorrowful for sin, humble, and teachable.

chapters.n: The consecration covenant at Thompson has been broken—Leman Copley withdrew the land he had promised—so the agreement is now void.

f.g: Cancelled; no longer binding.

chapters.n: Woe to the one responsible for this offense; it would have been better for him to drown in the sea. Jesus used similar words about those who cause others to stumble.

f.w: drowned in the depth of the sea

chapters.n: Those who kept the covenant and the commandment are blessed and will receive mercy.
So they must leave Thompson before their enemies come, choose a leader, and appoint someone to handle their money.

f.g: An old phrase meaning “come now” or “go ahead.”

chapters.n: They are to travel west to Missouri, to the border with the Native American lands.

f.g: The western edge of Missouri, beyond which lay Indian Territory.

chapters.n: Once there, they should earn a living like anyone else until the Lord prepares a place. Faith does not replace work.

f.w: seek ye a living like unto men
f.g: Support yourselves through ordinary work.

chapters.n: Be patient in trials until the Lord comes. He comes quickly, bringing reward, and those who sought him early will find rest for their souls.

William W. Phelps, a newspaper editor and printer, had come to Kirtland to learn God’s will for him. The Lord calls him and promises forgiveness and the Holy Ghost if he is baptized with pure motives.

f.g: William Wines Phelps (1792–1872), later the Church’s printer and author of many hymns, including “The Spirit of God.”

f.w: an eye single to my glory

chapters.n: After baptism, Joseph Smith will ordain him an elder to preach repentance and baptism in Jesus Christ’s name.

f.w: baptism in the name of Jesus Christ

chapters.n: He will have power to confer the Holy Ghost on those who are contrite.

f.w: you shall have power to give the Holy Spirit

chapters.n: He will help Oliver Cowdery with printing and with selecting and writing schoolbooks, so even children may be taught in ways pleasing to God. This is one of the earliest scriptural mandates for Church education.

f.g: Phelps later published the Church’s first newspaper and the Book of Commandments in Missouri.

chapters.n: For this purpose he will travel to Missouri with Joseph and Sidney and be “planted” in the land of inheritance.

f.g: Settled permanently.

chapters.n: Joseph Coe is also to go with them. More instructions will come later.

f.g: An early convert from New York who settled in Kirtland.

chapters.n: The Lord addresses all who claim his name, warning that his anger burns against the rebellious, who will feel his power in the coming day of judgment.

f.g: A time when God comes to judge or bless.

chapters.n: Anyone unwilling to take up the cross, follow Christ, and keep his commandments will not be saved. Discipleship involves sacrifice.

f.w: take up his cross and follow me

chapters.n: When the Lord commands and the command is broken, the disobedient will be cut off in his timing.
The Lord can command and revoke as he sees fit; responsibility for revoked blessings rests on the rebellious. God adjusts his instructions in response to human choices.
Because Ezra Thayre wouldn’t leave, the Lord revokes the pairing of Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra and sends Thomas with Selah J. Griffin instead.

f.w: Thomas B. Marsh and Ezra Thayre

chapters.n: The earlier pairing of Selah J. Griffin and Newel Knight is also revoked because of the stubbornness of the Saints in Thompson.

f.g: Stubbornness, unwillingness to bend.

chapters.n: Newel Knight is to stay and lead to Missouri any who are humble and willing.

f.w: the land which I have appointed

chapters.n: Ezra Thayre must repent of pride and selfishness and obey earlier instructions about the land where he lived—apparently a property dispute connected with Joseph Smith Sr.’s farm in Kirtland.

f.w: the place upon which he lives
f.g: A farm near Kirtland in which Ezra had invested money.

chapters.n: If he obeys—and the land is not divided—he may still go to Missouri.
Otherwise, he will get his money back, leave the land, and be removed from the Church.

f.g: Hosts = armies; the Lord as commander of heaven’s armies.

chapters.n: Though heaven and earth pass away, the Lord’s words will be fulfilled.

f.w: though the heaven and the earth pass away, these words shall not pass away

chapters.n: If Joseph Smith must refund Ezra’s money, the Lord will repay Joseph in Missouri, and those who give to him will be rewarded.
People will receive according to their deeds, even in lands of inheritance.

f.w: according to that which they do they shall receive

chapters.n: Turning to the Saints generally, the Lord says they have much to repent of; their sins remain unpardoned because they follow their own counsel rather than his.

f.w: you seek to counsel in your own ways

chapters.n: Their hearts are never satisfied; they disobey truth and take pleasure in wrongdoing.
Woe to the rich who refuse to share with the poor—their wealth will corrode their souls. In the judgment they will lament, in Jeremiah’s words, that the harvest is past and they are not saved.

f.g: Corrode or rust; eat away like a sore.

f.w: The harvest is past, the summer is ended

chapters.n: But woe also to the poor whose hearts are unbroken and greedy, who covet others’ goods and refuse to work. The Lord condemns attitudes, not economic status.

f.w: whose hands are not stayed from laying hold upon other men's goods
f.g: Who don’t hold back from grabbing other people’s things.

chapters.n: Blessed are the poor who are pure in heart, broken-hearted, and contrite; they will see God’s kingdom come in power to deliver them, and the earth’s riches will be theirs.

f.w: the poor who are pure in heart

f.g: The earth’s richest bounty.

chapters.n: The Lord will come with his reward, giving each person their due, and the poor will rejoice.

f.w: his recompense shall be with him

chapters.n: Their descendants will inherit the earth forever. The Lord ends his message.
After traveling about a thousand miles, the elders have gathered in Missouri. The Lord confirms that this is the land he has appointed and consecrated for gathering the Saints.
This is the land of promise and the site of the city of Zion—the New Jerusalem foretold in scripture.
Independence, in Jackson County, is the “center place.” A temple site lies west of the courthouse. Bishop Partridge purchased this temple lot later in 1831; Joseph Smith dedicated it that August.

f.g: A small frontier town in western Missouri, founded in 1827.

chapters.n: The Saints should buy land there and westward up to the boundary between “Jew and Gentile.” Many understand this as the border between Missouri and the Indian Territory, home to Native peoples whom the revelations count among Israel’s descendants.

f.w: the line running directly between Jew and Gentile
f.g: Likely the western Missouri state line, beyond which lived Native American tribes.

chapters.n: They should also buy land bordering the prairies, as they can afford, for an everlasting inheritance.
Sidney Gilbert is confirmed as Church agent to receive money and buy land in surrounding regions—always honestly and wisely.
Bishop Edward Partridge and his assistants are to divide the inheritances among the Saints, as commanded.

f.w: divide unto the saints their inheritance

chapters.n: Gilbert is to settle there and open a store, selling goods honestly, to raise money to buy land and supply the Saints’ needs.

f.g: Honestly, without deception.

chapters.n: He should obtain a license to trade, perhaps with Native peoples, and send goods through clerks he employs.

f.g: A government license, probably to trade with Native Americans beyond the frontier.

chapters.n: Thus the Saints will be provided for, and the gospel can reach those living in spiritual darkness.

f.w: the region and shadow of death

chapters.n: William W. Phelps is to settle there as the Church’s printer.
If the world accepts his writings, he may earn what he can honestly, for the good of the Saints.
Oliver Cowdery is to assist him in copying, correcting, and selecting materials so everything is right before God, as confirmed by the Spirit.

f.w: to copy, and to correct, and select
f.g: Editorial work on the revelations being prepared for publication.

chapters.n: These men are to move to Zion with their families as soon as possible.
Regarding the gathering: the bishop and agent must prepare for families commanded to come and settle them on their inheritances.
Other elders and members will receive further directions later.
The elders newly arrived in Missouri are told to listen and learn the Lord’s will for them and for this land. Some were disappointed by the rough frontier and the small number of Saints there.

f.w: this land unto which I have sent you

chapters.n: Those who keep the commandments are blessed, living or dead, and those faithful in hardship will receive greater reward in heaven.
For now, they cannot see with natural eyes God’s full plan or the glory that will come after much trouble. Faith trusts what cannot yet be seen.

f.g: Ordinary mortal perception, as opposed to spiritual sight.

chapters.n: A principle many have found comforting: blessings come after tribulation. Their crown of glory is coming—not yet, but soon.

f.w: after much tribulation come the blessings

chapters.n: He tells them in advance so they can take it to heart and be ready for what follows.

f.g: Take it seriously; remember it deeply.

chapters.n: They were sent to learn obedience and to prepare their hearts to testify of things to come.
They have the honor of laying Zion’s foundation and bearing witness of the land where it will stand.
Zion will provide a rich feast for the poor, fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy of a banquet of the finest food and well-aged wine—proof that the prophets’ words do not fail.

f.w: wine on the lees well refined
f.g: Wine aged on its sediment and then strained—the best quality.

chapters.n: It will be the Lord’s supper—a great banquet to which all nations are invited.

f.w: a supper of the house of the Lord

chapters.n: First the invitation goes to the rich, learned, wise, and noble.
Then, in the day of the Lord’s power, the poor, lame, blind, and deaf will come to the marriage feast of the Lamb—as in Jesus’s parable of the great supper.

f.w: the poor, the lame, and the blind

chapters.n: The Lord affirms that he has spoken it.
The testimony of the gospel is to go out from Zion, God’s city of inheritance.

f.w: the testimony might go forth from Zion

chapters.n: That’s why the Lord sent them and chose Edward Partridge for his work in Missouri.
Yet Edward must repent of unbelief and “blindness of heart”—he had questioned the choice of land—or risk falling.
His mission is given once and will not be given again.
The bishop is a judge in Israel, like judges in ancient Israel, who divides the land of inheritance among God’s children.
He judges fairly, using the testimony of the righteous and the help of counselors, following laws given through prophets.
God’s law will be kept in this land.
No leader should think he is the ruler; God must rule the one who judges. Leaders serve under God’s authority.

f.w: Let no man think he is ruler

chapters.n: Do not break the laws of the land; those who keep God’s laws have no need to.

f.w: Let no man break the laws of the land

chapters.n: Submit to the governing authorities until Christ, who has the right to rule, reigns and subdues all enemies.

f.w: be subject to the powers that be
he reigns whose right it is to reign

chapters.n: The laws they have received are Church laws and should be presented that way—not as civil laws imposed on others.
Missouri will be home to Edward Partridge, his counselors, and the storehouse keeper.

f.w: him whom I have appointed to keep my storehouse
f.g: Sidney Gilbert (D&C 57:6-8).

chapters.n: They should bring their families as they counsel among themselves and with the Lord.
The Lord does not want to command in everything. A servant who must be told everything is lazy and unwise and gains no reward.

f.g: Fitting, appropriate.
Lazy.

chapters.n: A famous principle: be anxiously engaged in good causes, doing much good on your own initiative. God values self-motivated righteousness.

f.w: anxiously engaged in a good cause
f.g: “Anxiously” here means eagerly, earnestly.

chapters.n: People have power within them to act as their own agents. Good done will never lose its reward.
But those who do nothing until commanded, obey with doubt, and comply lazily are condemned—their progress halted.

f.g: Condemned; stopped from progressing.

chapters.n: Can the Creator hold the disobedient guiltless? The Lord asks a rhetorical question.
Has the Lord ever failed to fulfill a promise? Another rhetorical question with an obvious answer.

f.w: have promised and have not fulfilled

chapters.n: When the Lord commands and people disobey, he revokes the promise, and they miss the blessing.
Then they blame God, saying the work isn’t his because the promises failed. Woe to them—their reward comes from below, not above.

f.g: Lies hidden, waiting.

chapters.n: The Lord now gives more directions about the land.
Martin Harris should set an example by consecrating his money to the bishop. He was among the first to sign a consecration deed in Missouri.

f.w: laying his moneys before the bishop

chapters.n: Anyone coming to receive an inheritance must likewise follow the law of consecration with his money.
Land should be bought in Independence for a storehouse and a printing office.

f.g: The printing office where W. W. Phelps published The Evening and the Morning Star.

chapters.n: Martin Harris will receive further direction by the Spirit regarding his inheritance.
Martin must repent, because he seeks the world’s praise.
William W. Phelps is confirmed in his calling and will receive an inheritance.

f.w: the office to which I have appointed him

chapters.n: Phelps too must repent: the Lord is displeased because he seeks to excel over others and is not meek enough.

f.g: He wants to stand above others.

chapters.n: One of scripture’s most comforting promises: whoever has repented is forgiven, and the Lord remembers those sins no more.
How do you know someone has repented? They confess their sins and forsake them.

f.w: he will confess them and forsake them

chapters.n: Most elders will not receive inheritances in Missouri for many years, unless the Lord appoints it through prayer.
They will “push the people together from the ends of the earth”—gather Israel—using Moses’s image of Joseph’s descendants gathering like a charging ox.

f.w: push the people together from the ends of the earth

chapters.n: So they should hold conference; those not staying should preach nearby, then return home.
Preach on the way, testifying everywhere, calling rich and poor alike to repent.
Organize branches wherever people repent.
An agent should be chosen for the Ohio Church to collect money for buying land in Zion.
Sidney Rigdon is to write a description of Zion and of God’s will, as the Spirit directs.

f.w: a description of the land of Zion

chapters.n: He will also write a letter and subscription appeal to all branches, raising money for the bishop or agent to buy land.

f.g: A letter and a pledge list for contributions.

chapters.n: The Lord wants people to open their hearts and buy the whole region as soon as possible.
Purchase is the way—otherwise inheritance could come only through bloodshed, which the Lord forbids.

f.w: save it be by the shedding of blood

chapters.n: As land is obtained, skilled workers of all kinds should be sent to labor for the Saints.
All must be done in order, with the bishop or agent announcing land available from time to time.
Gathering must not be hasty or like a flight, but organized according to counsel given in conferences.

f.w: not in haste, nor by flight

chapters.n: Sidney Rigdon is to dedicate the land and temple site to the Lord. He did so on August 2, 1831; Joseph dedicated the temple site the next day.

f.g: A formal prayer setting the land apart for the Lord’s purposes.

chapters.n: After a conference, Joseph, Sidney, and Oliver are to return to Ohio to finish their work there.
No one returning should travel silently; each must testify on the way of what he knows.
Ziba Peterson, a missionary to the Lamanites, loses his calling for unconfessed sins. He remains a member and must work until humbled.

f.g: One of the four missionaries sent to the Lamanites in 1830 (D&C 32:3).
Corrected through discipline.

chapters.n: The other elders coming to Missouri, some greatly blessed, should also hold a conference there.
Edward Partridge is to preside over that conference.
They too should return home preaching and testifying of what has been revealed.
The gospel’s sound must go from Zion to all the world, preached to every creature, with signs following believers.

f.w: preached unto every creature, with signs following them that believe

chapters.n: The revelation ends with a brief, solemn reminder: the Son of Man is coming.
Given on a Sabbath in Missouri, the day Polly Knight was buried, this revelation blesses those who came to Zion with pure motives and obedience.

f.w: an eye single to my glory

chapters.n: Those who live will inherit the earth; those who die will rest, their works following them, and receive a crown in the Father’s mansions. Polly Knight had prayed to see Zion before she died.
Those standing in Zion who obey the gospel will receive earth’s good things as it yields in full strength.
The faithful will also receive heavenly blessings, many commandments, and revelations in due time. More commandments are counted as a blessing, not a burden.

f.g: Many commandments.

chapters.n: The first great commandment: love God with all your heart, might, mind, and strength, and serve him in Jesus Christ’s name.

f.w: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God

chapters.n: The second: love your neighbor as yourself. Don’t steal, commit adultery, kill, or do anything like it—the spirit, not just the letter, of the law.

f.w: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself
nor do anything like unto it
f.g: Avoid not only the act but anything resembling it.

chapters.n: Thank God in all things—even trials.

f.w: thank the Lord thy God in all things

chapters.n: The sacrifice God wants is a broken heart and contrite spirit, which replaced animal sacrifices after Christ.

f.w: a broken heart and a contrite spirit

chapters.n: To stay unspotted from the world, go to the house of prayer and offer your sacraments on the Lord’s holy day. This is a key Sabbath scripture.
The Sabbath is appointed for rest from labor and devotion to God.

f.w: to pay thy devotions unto the Most High
f.g: To worship and give reverent attention to God.

chapters.n: Yet righteous devotion and vows to God belong to every day, not only Sunday.

f.g: Sacred promises or offerings to God.

chapters.n: On the Lord’s day especially, offer your oblations—offerings—and sacraments, and confess sins to fellow Saints and to the Lord.

f.g: Offerings to God of time, talents, or means.

chapters.n: Do no other work that day; prepare food with singleness of heart so your fasting may be perfect—or, in other words, your joy full.

f.g: Simple sincerity, focused on God.

chapters.n: The Lord explains that fasting and prayer are, in essence, rejoicing and prayer. True Sabbath observance is joyful.
Do these things with thanksgiving and cheerful faces—but not with excessive, frivolous laughter. A glad heart is different from shallow levity.
Do this and the fulness of the earth is yours: animals, birds, and creatures that climb and walk.

f.w: the fulness of the earth is yours

chapters.n: Plants and earth’s good things—for food, clothing, houses, barns, orchards, gardens, and vineyards—are yours too.

f.g: Plants in general.

chapters.n: Everything from the earth in its season is made for human use—both to please the eye and to gladden the heart. God created beauty, not just utility.

f.w: both to please the eye and to gladden the heart

chapters.n: For food, clothing, taste, and smell; to strengthen the body and enliven the soul.
God is pleased to give these gifts, but they must be used wisely—not to excess and not by extortion.

f.w: with judgment, not to excess, neither by extortion
f.g: With good sense, in moderation, and without exploiting others.

chapters.n: Nothing offends God more than failing to acknowledge his hand in all things and disobeying his commandments. Gratitude is central.

f.w: confess not his hand in all things

chapters.n: This is consistent with the law and the prophets; the Lord asks the Saints not to trouble him further about it.
Those who do righteous works will receive peace in this world and eternal life in the next—a well-loved promise.

f.w: peace in this world, and eternal life in the world to come

chapters.n: The Lord has spoken, and the Spirit testifies of it.
The elders preparing to return from Missouri to Ohio hear that the Lord is pleased they came to Zion.

f.w: return speedily to the land from whence they came

chapters.n: But some didn’t share the gospel on the journey out of fear of what people would think. Using Jesus’s parable, the Lord says they hid their talent—and he is displeased.
If they don’t become more faithful, even what they have will be taken away.

f.w: it shall be taken away, even that which they have

chapters.n: The Lord rules heaven and earth. When he gathers his “jewels”—his treasured people—everyone will recognize what reveals God’s power.

f.w: in the day when I shall make up my jewels

f.g: Shows, indicates.

chapters.n: For the trip home, they may build or buy a boat—it doesn’t matter to the Lord—and travel quickly down the Missouri River to St. Louis.

f.g: A boat, likely canoes, for river travel.

chapters.n: From St. Louis, Sidney, Joseph, and Oliver are to go to Cincinnati.
There they are to preach boldly, without anger or doubt, lifting holy hands. The Lord can make them holy, and their sins are forgiven.
The others should travel from St. Louis in pairs, preaching calmly among unbelievers until they reach home.

f.g: Without rushing past opportunities to teach.

chapters.n: This is for the benefit of the branches.
Bishop Partridge is to give the returning elders some money from what has been entrusted to him.
Those able to repay it should do so through the agent; those unable need not.
Now the Lord speaks of the elders still coming to Missouri.
They must not waste time or bury their talents, hiding what they have to offer.

f.w: neither shalt thou bury thy talent

chapters.n: After reaching Zion and preaching, they should return promptly, teaching on the way—without rushing, anger, or contention.

f.w: neither in wrath nor with strife

chapters.n: Shake the dust from your feet against those who reject you—privately, not to provoke them—and wash your feet as a testimony for the judgment.

f.w: shake off the dust of thy feet

chapters.n: This is enough instruction for now; it is the will of the one who sent them.
Joseph will reveal more about Sidney Rigdon and Oliver Cowdery; other matters will come later.
The all-powerful, eternal Lord speaks. The elders were camped at McIlwaine’s Bend on the Missouri River after a dangerous day; one of their canoes had nearly capsized on a submerged tree.
Their sins are forgiven; the Lord is merciful to those who humbly confess. Tension and quarreling had arisen among the travelers.
It isn’t necessary for all the elders to rush downriver while people on both banks perish in unbelief—they should be preaching.
The Lord allowed this journey so they could testify of the dangers on the waters, which will increase.

f.g: I allowed it.

chapters.n: In his anger, the Lord has decreed many destructions upon the waters, especially these.
Yet all flesh is in his hands, and the faithful will not perish by water.
Sidney Gilbert and William W. Phelps must hurry on their errand—they were heading to Ohio to obtain supplies and a press for Zion.
The Lord didn’t want them separated until they had been chastened and unified, so they would not perish in wickedness.
Now it is time to part. Gilbert and Phelps should take their original group and hurry, overcoming through faith.

f.g: It is right or necessary for me.

chapters.n: If faithful, they will be preserved, and the Lord will be with them.
The rest should take only needed clothing.
Gilbert should take the remaining items as agreed.
The Lord gave these commands for their good and will reason with them as with people of old.
In the beginning the Lord blessed the waters, but in the last days, through John the Revelator, he cursed them.

f.w: in the beginning blessed the waters
by the mouth of my servant John, I cursed the waters

chapters.n: Days will come when no one will be safe on the waters.
It will be said that only the upright in heart can travel to Zion by water.
As the Lord cursed the land after the Fall, so in the last days he has blessed it for the Saints to enjoy its richness.

f.w: in the beginning cursed the land

f.g: Its richness and abundance.

chapters.n: What he says to one, he says to all: warn others against traveling on these waters, lest their faith fail and they be caught in snares.
The Lord has decreed it: the destroyer rides upon the waters, and the decree stands.

f.g: Satan or a destroying power permitted by God.

chapters.n: He was angry with them yesterday, but today his anger has turned away. God’s anger is brief toward the repentant.

f.w: today mine anger is turned away

chapters.n: Those told to hurry should indeed hurry.
After a while, it won’t matter whether they go by water or land, as long as they fulfill their mission; they will judge as guided.
Joseph, Sidney, and Oliver are not to travel by water again except on the canal on their way home.

f.g: The Ohio and Erie Canal, which ran through Ohio toward Lake Erie.

chapters.n: The Lord sets the route for Saints traveling to Zion: after leaving the canal, they should go by land.
Like ancient Israel journeying to the promised land, they should pitch tents along the way.

f.w: like unto the children of Israel, pitching their tents

chapters.n: This commandment should be given to all the brethren.
Yet whoever is given power to command the waters will know by the Spirit how to proceed.
He should follow the Spirit, whether by land or by water.
They are given the route for the Saints—“the camp of the Lord”—to journey.

f.g: The Lord’s traveling people, echoing Israel’s camp in the wilderness.

chapters.n: Joseph, Sidney, and Oliver shouldn’t preach to unbelievers until they reach Cincinnati.
There they should raise their voices to God against a people nearly ripe for destruction.

f.g: Almost fully ripe in wickedness.

chapters.n: Then they should go to the branches, where they are needed more than among the wicked.
The others should preach among the wicked as they are able.
By doing so they rid their garments of others’ sins and stand spotless before God—a phrase meaning they have fulfilled their duty to warn.
They may travel together or in pairs, but Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel H. Smith must stay together until they return—for a wise purpose.
Be of good cheer, little children—the Lord is among them and has not forsaken them.
Because they have humbled themselves, the kingdom’s blessings are theirs.
Prepare, watch, and be serious-minded, looking for the Son of Man, who comes unexpectedly.

f.w: he cometh in an hour you think not

chapters.n: Pray always to avoid temptation and be ready for his coming, whether living or dead.

f.w: Pray always that you enter not into temptation

chapters.n: Jesus Christ, their advocate, addresses elders met on the Missouri River at Chariton. He understands human weakness and knows how to help those who are tempted.

f.g: Help, come to the aid of.

chapters.n: These elders haven’t yet reached Zion, so their mission isn’t complete.
Still, they are blessed: their testimonies are recorded in heaven for angels to see, angels rejoice over them, and their sins are forgiven. Testimony borne is never wasted.
They should continue to Zion, meet together, rejoice, and partake of the sacrament.

f.g: Partake of the Lord’s supper or offer worship.

chapters.n: Afterward they may return together or in pairs—it doesn’t matter—only be faithful and share the good news.

f.g: Good news—the gospel.

chapters.n: The Lord brought them together so the faithful could rejoice together in Missouri. He promises, and he cannot lie.
Anyone who wishes may ride horses, mules, or carriages for the return, as a gift from the Lord received with thanks.

f.g: Wagons or carriages.

chapters.n: These choices are left to their judgment and the Spirit’s guidance. The Lord trusts their agency.
The kingdom is theirs, and the Lord is always with the faithful.

f.w: I am with the faithful always

chapters.n: Back in Kirtland in late August 1831, the Saints were eager to hear about Zion. The Lord calls everyone who claims to be his people to open their hearts and hear his will.

f.g: Listen, even from a distance.

chapters.n: This is the voice of the One whose anger burns against the wicked and rebellious.
He decides who is taken in death and who is preserved in life. Life and death are in his hands.

f.w: take even them whom he will take

chapters.n: He builds and destroys at his will and has power to cast the soul into hell. Jesus taught that we should fear God rather than people.

f.w: able to cast the soul down to hell

chapters.n: When the Lord speaks, his word will be obeyed.

f.w: I, the Lord, utter my voice

chapters.n: The wicked should take heed, the rebellious tremble, and unbelievers stop scoffing, for wrath will come like a whirlwind and all will know he is God.

f.g: Keep quiet; stop speaking against God.

chapters.n: Those who seek signs will see them—but signs alone will not save them.
Some among the Saints seek signs, as people have from the beginning. Ezra Booth, for one, had joined after seeing a healing and later left in disappointment.
A key principle: faith does not come from signs; signs follow those who believe.
Signs come by faith and according to God’s will—not on human demand.

f.w: not by the will of men

chapters.n: Signs and mighty works flow from faith, for without faith no one pleases God. To those he is displeased with, he shows signs only in judgment.

f.w: without faith no man pleaseth God

chapters.n: The Lord is displeased with those who seek signs to build their faith rather than to bless others and glorify God.
He gives commandments, yet many have turned away from them.
There were adulterers and adulteresses among the Saints; some have left, and others still among them will be exposed.
Let them repent quickly, before judgment catches them like a trap and their foolishness becomes public.

f.g: Like a hidden trap.

chapters.n: Lust and adultery in the heart drive away the Spirit, lead to denying the faith, and bring fear. Moral purity and spiritual strength are tied together.

f.w: he that looketh on a woman to lust after her

chapters.n: Echoing Revelation, the Lord lists those who face the “second death”—spiritual separation from God: the fearful, unbelievers, liars, the sexually immoral, and sorcerers.

f.w: that lake which burneth with fire and brimstone, which is the second death

f.g: A sexually immoral person.

chapters.n: Such people will not rise in the first resurrection, which is for the righteous.
The Church as a whole is not justified while these sins remain among them.
But whoever endures in faith and does God’s will will overcome and inherit the earth in the day of transfiguration.

f.g: When the earth is renewed and glorified at Christ’s coming.
