chapters.n: The earth will be transfigured in a way shown to Peter, James, and John on the Mount of Transfiguration—though the full account has not yet been revealed.

f.w: the pattern which was shown unto mine apostles upon the mount

chapters.n: The Lord will make his will known—not as a commandment, since many ignore commandments.
To those who keep his commandments, he reveals the mysteries of his kingdom, which become a well of living water springing up to eternal life.

f.w: a well of living water, springing up unto everlasting life

chapters.n: The Saints are to gather to Zion—but not in haste, which brings confusion and disease.

f.g: Deadly disease.

chapters.n: The Lord holds the land of Zion in his own hands.

f.w: I, the Lord, hold it in mine own hands

chapters.n: Yet he renders to Caesar what is Caesar’s—respecting civil law and property rights.

f.w: render unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar's

chapters.n: So the Saints must buy the land, giving them a legal claim and avoiding provoking their neighbors.

f.w: that you may have advantage of the world
f.g: Here, a lawful standing or claim in the eyes of the world.

chapters.n: Satan stirs people’s hearts to anger and bloodshed against them.
Zion can be obtained only by purchase or by blood.
If by purchase, the Saints are blessed.
If by blood—which they are forbidden to shed—their enemies will drive them from city to city, and few will remain. This sadly anticipated their expulsion from Jackson County in 1833.
The Lord is angry with the wicked and is withdrawing his Spirit from the earth’s inhabitants.
He has decreed wars on the earth—the wicked will kill the wicked, and fear will grip everyone.

f.w: the wicked shall slay the wicked

chapters.n: The Saints will barely escape, but the Lord will be with them and come down from his Father’s presence to destroy the wicked.

f.w: the saints also shall hardly escape

chapters.n: This is not yet—but it will come.

f.g: Later; in time.

chapters.n: Because these judgments are coming, the Lord wants his Saints gathered in Zion.
Every person should hold righteousness in his hands, wear faithfulness like a belt, and warn the world—by words and even by leaving—that desolation is coming.
The disciples in Kirtland living on “this farm”—the Isaac Morley farm—should arrange their affairs.

f.g: Isaac Morley’s farm near Kirtland, where many Saints had settled and lived communally.

chapters.n: Titus Billings, who manages the farm, should sell the land and prepare to move to Zion in spring with its residents, except those the Lord keeps back.

f.g: An early convert and Isaac Morley’s brother-in-law; he led a company to Missouri in 1832.

chapters.n: All money that can be spared, whether little or much, should be sent to Zion.
Joseph Smith will be given power to discern by the Spirit who should go to Zion and who should stay.

f.g: Stay, remain.

chapters.n: Newel K. Whitney should keep his store for a little while.

f.g: A Kirtland merchant; his store became an important Church center.

chapters.n: But he should send all the money he can to Zion.
These things are in his hands; he should act wisely.
He is to be appointed as an agent for the disciples who remain in Kirtland.
He and Oliver Cowdery should visit the branches quickly, explaining these things and raising funds.

f.g: Explaining in detail.

chapters.n: Those who are faithful and endure will overcome the world.
Those who send treasures to Zion will receive an inheritance here and a reward in the world to come.
Blessed are those who die in the Lord: at his coming, when all things become new, they will rise, never die again, and receive an inheritance in the holy city.

f.w: blessed are the dead that die in the Lord

chapters.n: Those alive at his coming who kept the faith are blessed, yet they will still “die” at an advanced age.
During the Millennium, children will grow old, and the old will be changed in an instant from mortality to immortality rather than lying in the grave.

f.w: changed in the twinkling of an eye

chapters.n: This is why the apostles preached the resurrection.
Speaking in the Lord’s way of time, these things are near and will come at the Son of Man’s coming.

f.w: speaking after the manner of the Lord
f.g: Measured by God’s timeframe, not ours.

chapters.n: Until then, foolish virgins will live among the wise; at his coming, the righteous and wicked will be fully separated.
The Lord is displeased with Sidney Rigdon: he became proud, rejected counsel, and grieved the Spirit.
So his description of Zion is unacceptable; he must write another, or lose his office.
Those who meekly desire to warn sinners may be ordained to do so.
This is a day of warning, not of many words. God will not be mocked in the last days.
The Lord is above all and his power reaches beneath; he is over, in, and through all things, and searches everything.

f.w: over all, and in all, and through all

chapters.n: He identifies himself: Alpha and Omega, Jesus Christ.
Therefore, people should be careful how they speak his name.
Many are condemned for using the Lord’s name in vain—speaking or acting in it without authority.
The Church must repent, and the Lord will claim them as his own; otherwise they will be cut off.

f.g: Acknowledge or claim as his.

chapters.n: What comes from heaven is sacred and must be spoken carefully, under the Spirit’s direction, which comes through prayer. Without that, there is condemnation.

f.g: When the Spirit prompts or compels.

f.w: that which cometh from above is sacred

chapters.n: Joseph and Sidney should seek homes, as the Spirit teaches through prayer. They soon moved to Hiram, Ohio.
These challenges are to be overcome through patience, bringing a “more exceeding and eternal weight of glory”—or greater condemnation if not.

f.w: a more exceeding and eternal weight of glory

chapters.n: The Lord speaks to the elders in Kirtland in September 1831, shortly before Joseph moved to Hiram. Some had returned from Missouri with hard feelings toward one another.
He wants them to overcome the world, and so he will show them compassion.
Some among them have sinned, but this once, for his glory and their salvation, he has forgiven them.
He will be merciful because he has given them the kingdom.
The keys of the kingdom’s mysteries will remain with Joseph Smith while he lives, as long as he obeys.

f.w: the keys of the mysteries of the kingdom

chapters.n: Some have looked for reasons to accuse Joseph without cause.

f.g: Looked for an excuse to criticize or accuse him.

chapters.n: Joseph has sinned too, but the Lord forgives all who confess and seek forgiveness, unless they have sinned “unto death.” Prophets are not perfect.
The Lord’s disciples of old held grudges against one another and suffered for it.

f.g: Severely disciplined.

chapters.n: Therefore forgive one another. Whoever refuses to forgive carries “the greater sin.” Unforgiveness hurts the one who withholds it.

f.w: ye ought to forgive one another

chapters.n: One of the best-known verses on forgiveness: the Lord will forgive whom he will, but we are required to forgive everyone.

f.w: of you it is required to forgive all men

chapters.n: Instead of holding grudges, say in your heart: let God judge between us and repay according to deeds. Leaving judgment to God frees the heart.

f.w: let God judge between me and thee

chapters.n: Unrepentant sinners who won’t confess should still be brought before the Church as scripture directs.
This is done not from lack of compassion but to glorify God and honor his law. Forgiveness and accountability work together.
This is the reason they are to do these things.
The Lord was angry with Ezra Booth and Isaac Morley for not keeping the law. Booth had since left the Church.

f.w: him who was my servant Ezra Booth
f.g: “Who was” signals Booth had apostatized; he wrote critical letters published in an Ohio newspaper.

chapters.n: They looked for faults and condemned what wasn’t evil, so the Spirit withdrew. Yet Isaac Morley has been forgiven.
Edward Partridge has also sinned, and Satan seeks his soul—but if he and others repent when shown their error, they will be forgiven.
Sidney Gilbert should return to his agency in Zion after a few weeks.
He should share what he has seen and heard, so the disciples don’t perish.
Isaac Morley’s farm was ordered sold so he wouldn’t be tempted beyond his strength or give harmful counsel.

f.w: tempted above that which he is able to bear

chapters.n: Frederick G. Williams should not sell his farm, because the Lord wants a strong foothold in Kirtland for five years to save some. The Church did remain strong in Kirtland until 1838.

f.g: A physician who later served as a counselor in the First Presidency.

chapters.n: After that, no one will be held guilty for going to Zion with an open heart. The Lord requires people’s hearts.

f.w: I, the Lord, require the hearts of the children of men

chapters.n: “Today” lasts until Christ comes. It is a day of sacrifice and tithing; those who are tithed will not be burned at his coming. In 1831 “tithing” referred broadly to offerings; the specific law came in 1838.

f.w: he that is tithed shall not be burned

chapters.n: After “today” comes the burning: the proud and wicked will be like stubble. No one remaining in Babylon will be spared.

f.g: Dry stalks left after harvest—quick to burn.
Symbol of worldliness and wickedness.

chapters.n: If they believe him, they will work while it is still today.

f.w: labor while it is called today

chapters.n: Newel K. Whitney and Sidney Gilbert should not sell their store yet, until the remaining Church members in Kirtland move to Zion.
The Lord’s law forbids going into debt to enemies.

f.w: to get in debt to thine enemies
f.g: Being indebted to hostile people gives them power over you.

chapters.n: But the Lord himself may take and pay as he sees fit.
As agents, they are on the Lord’s errand; whatever they do by his will is his business.

f.g: Doing the Lord’s work as his representatives.

chapters.n: He has set them to provide for the Saints so they can obtain an inheritance in Zion.
The Lord’s words are sure: they will obtain it.
But everything must happen in its time.
A beloved verse: don’t grow weary in doing good, for you are laying the foundation of a great work. Great things grow from small ones.

f.w: out of small things proceedeth that which is great

chapters.n: The Lord requires the heart and a willing mind. The willing and obedient will enjoy the good of Zion.

f.w: the willing and obedient shall eat the good of the land

chapters.n: The rebellious will be removed from Zion and will not inherit it.
The rebellious are not truly of Ephraim’s blood—the covenant lineage entrusted with the gathering.

f.g: Ephraim, son of Joseph, whose descendants carry special responsibility in the latter-day gathering.

chapters.n: The Church is like a judge sitting on a hill, an elevated place, to judge the nations.

f.w: a judge sitting on a hill

chapters.n: Zion’s inhabitants will judge matters pertaining to Zion.
Liars and hypocrites will be exposed, and false apostles and prophets made known.

f.w: they who are not apostles and prophets

chapters.n: Even the bishop and his counselors will be condemned and replaced if unfaithful. No calling exempts anyone.

f.w: the bishop, who is a judge

chapters.n: Zion will flourish, and the Lord’s glory will rest on her.

f.w: the glory of the Lord shall be upon her

chapters.n: She will be an ensign—a banner—to the world, and people from every nation will come.

f.g: A flag or banner to rally around.

chapters.n: Nations will tremble because of her and fear her “terrible ones”—those made awe-inspiring by God’s power.

f.g: Awe-inspiring people, mighty through God.

chapters.n: Joseph Smith called this revelation a prayer. It opens with a mighty heavenly voice echoing John the Baptist and Isaiah: prepare the way of the Lord and make his paths straight.

f.w: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight

chapters.n: The keys—priesthood authority to direct God’s kingdom—are on earth again. From here the gospel will roll forth like the stone in Daniel’s vision, cut from the mountain without hands, until it fills the whole earth.

f.w: The keys of the kingdom of God are committed unto man
the stone which is cut out of the mountain without hands

chapters.n: The voice cries again: prepare for the Lord, prepare the Lamb’s wedding supper, and be ready for the Bridegroom—Christ.
Pray to the Lord, call on his holy name, and tell the world about his wonderful works.

f.w: make known his wonderful works among the people

chapters.n: Pray that God’s kingdom spreads across the earth so people can be ready when the Son of Man comes in glory to meet the kingdom set up on earth.

f.w: to meet the kingdom of God which is set up on the earth
f.g: The Church on earth (kingdom of God) prepares for the Millennial reign (kingdom of heaven).

chapters.n: The prayer ends echoing the Lord’s Prayer: may God’s kingdom go forth so heaven’s kingdom can come, and God be glorified on earth as in heaven.

f.w: that the kingdom of heaven may come

chapters.n: William E. McLellin, a schoolteacher baptized that summer, had secretly prayed for answers to five questions. The Lord blesses him for turning from sin and accepting the truth. McLellin later testified this revelation answered all his questions.

f.g: Later one of the original Twelve Apostles (1835); he left the Church in 1838.

chapters.n: He is blessed for receiving the everlasting covenant—the fulness of the gospel—which brings life and glories foretold by ancient prophets and apostles.
He is clean, but not entirely; he must repent of what displeases the Lord, who will show him what it is.

f.w: you are clean, but not all

chapters.n: The Lord will reveal his will for William.
He is to preach the gospel from land to land and city to city, especially where it hasn’t been preached.
Don’t stay long here or go to Zion yet. Send what you can there, but don’t worry about property.

f.g: Don’t stay long.

chapters.n: Go to the eastern states, testify everywhere, reasoning with people in their places of worship.

f.g: Here, churches or meeting places.

chapters.n: Samuel H. Smith should go with him; William must not abandon him, but should teach him. The faithful will be strengthened, and the Lord will go with them.
Bless the sick, and they will recover. Don’t return until sent. Be patient in trials. Ask and knock.

f.w: Lay your hands upon the sick, and they shall recover

chapters.n: Avoid being weighed down by distractions; forsake unrighteousness; don’t commit adultery—a temptation William had struggled with. The Lord knows each person’s specific weaknesses.

f.g: Burdened or weighed down with cares.

chapters.n: Keep these words; magnify your calling; and you will push many people to Zion singing songs of everlasting joy.

f.g: Fulfill one’s calling fully and honorably.

chapters.n: Continue faithfully to the end and receive a crown of eternal life at the Father’s right hand.
The revelation is signed by Jesus Christ, the Redeemer.
At a November 1831 conference in Hiram, Ohio, the elders were preparing to publish the revelations as the Book of Commandments. The Lord says he knows their prayers, hearts, and desires.
His eyes are on them; heaven and earth are in his hands, and eternity’s riches are his to give.
They tried to believe they would receive a promised blessing, but fear in their hearts kept them from it. Fear blocks faith.

f.w: there were fears in your hearts

chapters.n: Now the Lord gives them a testimony of the truth of the revelations before them.

f.w: these commandments which are lying before you
f.g: The manuscript of revelations prepared for publication.

chapters.n: They knew Joseph’s language and imperfections, and some wished they could express things better than he did.

f.g: Joseph had little formal schooling; some elders questioned the plain language of the revelations.

chapters.n: So the Lord issues a challenge: let the wisest among them try to write a revelation equal to the least of these. William E. McLellin made the attempt and failed.

f.g: The first printed collection of revelations, typeset in Missouri in 1833 before a mob destroyed the press.

chapters.n: If anyone succeeds, they would be justified in doubting.
But if not, they are condemned if they don’t testify the revelations are true. Several elders afterward signed a written testimony.
They know there is nothing unrighteous in the revelations, and righteousness comes from above, from the Father of lights.
A remarkable promise: if they strip away jealousy and fear and humble themselves, the veil will part and they will see the Lord—with spiritual, not natural, eyes.

f.g: Worldly, fleshly; unspiritual.

chapters.n: No one has seen God in the flesh except when “quickened” by his Spirit.

f.g: Made alive or spiritually enabled.

chapters.n: No natural person can endure God’s presence with a worldly mind.
They aren’t yet able to endure God’s presence or angelic ministry, so they must be patient until perfected.

f.w: continue in patience until ye are perfected

chapters.n: Don’t turn back. When worthy, in God’s timing, they will see and understand what was conferred on them through Joseph—the high priesthood conferred that year.

f.w: Let not your minds turn back

chapters.n: Orson Hyde, a recent convert and former Campbellite preacher, was ordained to preach the gospel by the Spirit everywhere, reasoning with people and explaining the scriptures.

f.g: Later one of the original Twelve Apostles; he dedicated the land of Palestine in 1841.
Explaining in detail.

chapters.n: His call is an example for all ordained to this priesthood and sent to preach.

f.g: Example or pattern.

chapters.n: The pattern: they must speak as the Holy Ghost moves them.

f.w: moved upon by the Holy Ghost

chapters.n: A significant verse: whatever they speak when moved by the Holy Ghost is scripture—the Lord’s will, mind, word, and voice, and God’s power to save. Revelation continues through inspired servants.

f.g: In Latter-day Saint usage, inspired words for their setting; formally canonized scripture is a narrower category.

f.w: the power of God unto salvation

chapters.n: This is the Lord’s promise to his servants.
Be of good cheer and don’t fear; the Lord stands by them. They will testify that Jesus is the Son of God—who was, is, and is to come.

f.w: I was, that I am, and that I am to come

chapters.n: This message goes to Orson Hyde, Luke Johnson, Lyman Johnson, William E. McLellin, and all faithful elders. All four later became members of the original Quorum of the Twelve.

f.g: Luke and Lyman Johnson were sons of John Johnson, in whose Hiram home Joseph was living.

chapters.n: Echoing the Great Commission: go into all the world, preach to everyone, and baptize in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

f.w: Go ye into all the world, preach the gospel to every creature

chapters.n: Those who believe and are baptized will be saved; those who don’t will be condemned.

f.w: he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved

chapters.n: Signs will follow believers, as scripture promises.
They will understand the signs of the times and of Christ’s coming.
They will have power to seal up to eternal life those the Father testifies of—a reference to high priesthood authority.

f.w: seal them up unto eternal life

chapters.n: The revelation now adds items to the Church’s covenants and commandments (D&C 20).
More bishops will be called in due time, serving as the first one (Edward Partridge) does.
Bishops will be worthy high priests appointed by the First Presidency—unless they are literal descendants of Aaron.

f.g: Organized in 1832–33; this wording reflects editing of the revelation before its 1835 publication.

chapters.n: A literal, firstborn descendant of Aaron has a legal right to the bishopric.
The firstborn holds the right of presidency over the Aaronic Priesthood.
Only a literal firstborn descendant of Aaron has an inherent legal right to this office and its keys.
But a Melchizedek high priest can act in all lesser offices, so he may serve as bishop when no such descendant is found, if called by the First Presidency.

f.w: officiate in all the lesser offices

chapters.n: Even a descendant of Aaron must be designated, found worthy, and ordained by this Presidency to serve legally.
Because priesthood rights pass from father to son, such descendants may claim their anointing if they prove their lineage or learn it by revelation under the Presidency’s direction.
Bishops and high priests set apart for this work may be tried only before the First Presidency.
If found guilty by unimpeachable testimony, they will be condemned.

f.g: Challenged or discredited.

chapters.n: If they repent, they will be forgiven according to Church covenants.
A cornerstone verse on parenting: parents in Zion who fail to teach their children faith in Christ, repentance, baptism, and the gift of the Holy Ghost by age eight bear the sin.

f.g: The age of accountability, when children may be baptized.

f.w: the sin be upon the heads of the parents

chapters.n: This is law for Zion and her organized stakes.

f.g: Like tent stakes supporting Zion’s tent, these are organized local units of the Church.

chapters.n: Children are to be baptized at eight and receive the laying on of hands.

f.w: baptized for the remission of their sins

chapters.n: Parents should also teach children to pray and live uprightly.
Zion’s people are to keep the Sabbath holy.

f.w: observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy

chapters.n: They must work faithfully at their appointed labors; the Lord takes note of idlers.
The Lord is displeased with Zion: there are idlers, children growing up in wickedness, and greed instead of seeking eternal riches.

f.w: their eyes are full of greediness

chapters.n: These problems must end. Oliver Cowdery is to carry this message to Zion.
Those who neglect their prayers at the proper times are to be brought to the attention of the bishop, the judge of the Lord’s people.

f.g: At the proper time.
The bishop (D&C 58:17).

chapters.n: These words are true and faithful; don’t break them or take away from them.
The Lord, Alpha and Omega, is coming quickly.
For Oliver Cowdery’s sake, it isn’t wise for him to carry the revelations and Church money to Missouri alone; a faithful companion should go. The trip was long and dangerous.

f.g: The revelations for printing and funds collected for Zion.

chapters.n: John Whitmer is assigned to accompany Oliver.
He should keep writing a history of important events in the Church.
He should receive counsel and help from Oliver and others.
Missionaries abroad should send reports of their stewardships to Zion.
Zion will be the center where all these records are received and kept.

f.g: A center or headquarters.

chapters.n: John should travel often among the branches to gather information.
He should preach, explain, write, copy, select, and gather whatever benefits the Church and future generations growing up in Zion. History serves the rising generation.
The Lord addresses Zion and distant Church members, giving a commandment to Joseph Smith, Martin Harris, Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps.

f.g: Saints gathering in Jackson County, Missouri.

chapters.n: He calls attention to his commandment for them.
He has appointed them stewards over the revelations, present and future. This group came to be known as the Literary Firm.

f.g: Responsible for publishing and managing the revelations.

chapters.n: They will account for this stewardship at judgment.
Their business is to manage the revelations and their profits.
They should not simply hand over these things to the Church or the world, but manage them responsibly.
Any surplus beyond their needs goes to the Lord’s storehouse.
Benefits are consecrated to Zion’s people and their descendants who become heirs by the kingdom’s laws.
This is what the Lord requires of everyone in their stewardship.
No one in the Church is exempt.
Not the bishop, the storehouse keeper, or anyone managing temporal affairs.
Those who serve in spiritual matters are worthy of their hire, just like those managing temporal affairs.
Indeed, more so—an abundance multiplied through spiritual blessings.
Yet in temporal things they must be equal—and willingly, not grudgingly—or the Spirit’s abundant blessings will be withheld. Economic unity and spiritual power are linked.

f.g: Reluctantly, resentfully.

chapters.n: This commandment benefits them: a sign of God’s blessings, a reward for diligence, and security.
It provides food, clothing, inheritance, homes, and lands wherever the Lord sends them.
They have been faithful in much and have done well when they have avoided sin.
The Lord is merciful and will bless them, and they will enter into joy.

In December 1831, former member Ezra Booth was publishing hostile letters in an Ohio newspaper. The Lord tells Joseph and Sidney to pause the Bible translation and preach, explaining the gospel from the scriptures as the Spirit gives power.

f.w: expounding the mysteries thereof out of the scriptures

chapters.n: They should preach in the surrounding regions and in the Church for a season, until told otherwise.

f.w: for the space of a season
f.g: For a limited time.

chapters.n: This is a temporary mission. They returned to translating about a month later (D&C 73).
Work in the vineyard, testify, and prepare the way for revelations still to come.
Whoever reads this should understand and accept it.
Those who receive will be given more—even power.

f.w: unto him that receiveth it shall be given more abundantly

chapters.n: Confront critics openly; invite them to discuss publicly or privately. Faithfulness will expose their shame. The Lord answers criticism with truth, not silence.

f.g: Confound = refute, leave without an answer.

chapters.n: Let opponents bring their strongest arguments against the Lord.
A precious promise from Isaiah: no weapon formed against them will prosper.

f.w: no weapon that is formed against you shall prosper

chapters.n: Anyone who speaks against them will be confounded in God’s timing.
Keep the commandments, which are true and faithful.
The Lord speaks to high priests gathered in Kirtland in December 1831, to whom the kingdom and power have been given.

f.w: the high priests of my church
f.g: The office of high priest was first conferred in June 1831.

chapters.n: It is time to appoint a bishop for the Church in Ohio, alongside Edward Partridge in Missouri.

f.w: this part of the Lord's vineyard
f.g: The Kirtland, Ohio, area.

chapters.n: They acted wisely in seeking this, because every steward must account for his stewardship, now and in eternity.

f.w: render an account of his stewardship

chapters.n: Whoever is faithful and wise in this life is counted worthy of mansions prepared by the Father.

f.w: the mansions prepared for him of my Father

chapters.n: Elders in Ohio will report their stewardship to the bishop appointed there.
These records are to be sent to the bishop in Zion.
The bishop’s duties are defined by revelation and by conference decisions.
Newel K. Whitney is called as bishop. He hesitated, feeling inadequate, but accepted after being reassured by the Lord.
Additional instructions now describe the bishop’s duties.
He is to keep the Lord’s storehouse and receive Church funds in the area.
He takes account of the elders and supplies their needs; those who can pay should.
Those payments are consecrated to help the poor and needy.
For those unable to pay, a record is sent to the bishop in Zion, who covers the debt from the Lord’s resources.
The spiritual labors of faithful missionaries count as payment of this debt.
So it comes from the Church as a whole, since everyone going to Zion must consecrate all to the bishop there.

f.w: lay all things before the bishop

chapters.n: Every elder in Ohio must account to the local bishop.
A certificate from the Ohio bishop to the bishop in Zion makes a person acceptable for an inheritance as a wise and faithful steward.

f.g: An early form of what Latter-day Saints now call a recommend.

chapters.n: Without it, he won’t be accepted by the bishop in Zion.
Every elder reporting to the bishop should be recommended by the branches where he labors.
Stewards of the Church’s literary concerns may seek help from bishops.
So that the revelations can be published worldwide and generate funds to benefit the Church.
They too must prove themselves wise stewards.
This pattern applies to all branches of the Church everywhere.

f.g: Example or pattern.

chapters.n: Additional instructions for members called or permitted to move to Zion.
They must carry a certificate from three elders or from the bishop.
Otherwise they won’t be considered wise stewards. This too is a pattern.
The elders who were preaching should continue preaching and encouraging nearby branches until the upcoming conference (held in Amherst, Ohio, later that January).

f.g: Earnest encouragement.

chapters.n: At the conference, their individual missions will be announced.

f.w: by the voice of the conference

chapters.n: Joseph and Sidney should resume translating the Bible.

f.g: Joseph Smith’s inspired revision of the Bible (the JST), paused in December 1831.

chapters.n: Where practical, they should preach until the conference, then continue translating until finished. The main work was completed in July 1833.
This is a pattern for the elders until further instruction.
No more for now. Prepare for action and be serious.

f.w: Gird up your loins and be sober

chapters.n: This revelation explains 1 Corinthians 7:14, which Joseph was studying in his Bible translation. Paul says a believing spouse sanctifies an unbelieving one, so their children are holy.

f.w: the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife

chapters.n: In the apostles’ time, Jews who rejected Jesus still practiced circumcision under the law of Moses.

f.g: The covenant rite given to Abraham’s male descendants.

chapters.n: Conflict arose when an unbelieving Jewish husband wanted his children circumcised and raised under the law of Moses, which Christ had fulfilled.
Children raised under the law then followed their fathers’ traditions, rejected Christ, and became “unholy.”
So Paul advised, on his own counsel rather than by direct command from the Lord, that believers not marry unbelievers unless the law of Moses was set aside in the home.

f.w: not of the Lord, but of himself

chapters.n: This would allow children to remain uncircumcised and end the tradition that young children are unholy.
The key truth: little children are holy, sanctified by Christ’s Atonement. They need no ritual to be made clean.
At a January 1832 conference in Amherst, Ohio, the Lord speaks through his Spirit, identifying himself as Alpha and Omega.
He addresses elders who volunteered to preach and “prune” his vineyard—clearing away what is unfruitful so good growth can flourish.
Go without delay, don’t be idle, work with all your strength.
Preach boldly, like a trumpet blast, according to revelation.

f.w: as with the sound of a trump

chapters.n: The faithful will be loaded with many sheaves—converts—and crowned with honor, glory, immortality, and eternal life.
The Lord revokes William E. McLellin’s earlier call to the eastern states.

f.w: the commission which I gave unto him

chapters.n: He gives him a new call, correcting him for his complaining. McLellin had cut short his mission with Samuel Smith.

f.g: Grumbling complaints.

chapters.n: He sinned but is forgiven and sent to the southern states.
Luke Johnson is to go with him.
They should pray for the Comforter, who will teach them what they need.

f.w: the Comforter, which shall teach them all things

chapters.n: Pray always so they don’t give up, and the Lord will be with them to the end.

f.w: Praying always that they faint not

f.g: Lose heart; give up.

chapters.n: This is the Lord’s will for them.
Orson Hyde and Samuel H. Smith are sent east; the Lord will be with them if faithful. They traveled through New England in 1832.
Lyman Johnson and Orson Pratt are also sent east, with the Lord’s presence promised.

f.w: I am with them also, even unto the end

chapters.n: Asa Dodds and Calves Wilson are sent west.
The faithful will overcome all and be raised up at the last day.

f.w: lifted up at the last day

chapters.n: Major N. Ashley and Burr Riggs are sent south.
All should travel house to house, village to village, city to city.
Leave a blessing on every home that welcomes them.

f.w: leave your blessing upon that house

chapters.n: Leave quickly from homes that reject them, shaking off the dust as a testimony against them.

f.w: shake off the dust of your feet

chapters.n: They will be filled with joy, and at judgment they will witness against that house.
It will be more bearable for the heathen at judgment than for those who rejected the message. Stay ready and faithful to overcome and be lifted up.

f.g: Those who never knew God’s law.

chapters.n: Now the Lord speaks to elders seeking his will.
The Church must help support missionaries’ families. Those who stay home share in the work by sustaining those who go.
Elders should find places for their families as fellow Saints are willing to help.
Those whose families are provided for should go and preach in any direction.
Ask and knock; the Comforter will show them where to go.

f.w: ask and they shall receive, knock and it shall be opened

chapters.n: Anyone who must provide for his family should do so—he will not lose his crown—and serve in the Church locally. Caring for family is also service to God.
Everyone should be diligent; idlers have no place in the Church unless they repent.

f.w: the idler shall not have place

chapters.n: Simeon Carter and Emer Harris are paired as missionary companions. Emer was Martin Harris’s brother.
Ezra Thayre and Thomas B. Marsh are paired—finally serving together as first planned.

f.w: Ezra Thayre and my servant Thomas B. Marsh

chapters.n: Hyrum Smith and Reynolds Cahoon are paired.
Daniel Stanton and Seymour Brunson are paired.
Sylvester Smith and Gideon Carter are paired.
Ruggles Eames and Stephen Burnett are paired.
Micah B. Welton and Eden Smith are paired. Each pairing reflects the Lord’s pattern of sending missionaries two by two.

This vision, received in the John Johnson home in Hiram, Ohio, opens with a hymn of praise. Like Isaiah, it calls heaven and earth to listen and rejoice: the Lord is God, and there is no other Savior.

f.w: Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth
beside him there is no Savior

chapters.n: God’s wisdom is great and his ways marvelous; no one can trace the full extent of his works.

f.w: the extent of his doings none can find out

chapters.n: His purposes never fail, and no one can stop his hand.

f.g: Hold back or stop his power.

chapters.n: He is unchanging through all eternity.

f.w: From eternity to eternity he is the same

chapters.n: The Lord is merciful and gracious to those who revere him and delights to honor those who serve him faithfully to the end.
Their reward will be great, their glory eternal.
To them he will reveal all the hidden mysteries of his kingdom, past and future.

f.w: all the hidden mysteries of my kingdom

chapters.n: They will know the wonders of eternity and things to come for many generations.
Their wisdom will be great and reach heaven, while worldly wisdom will perish.

f.w: the wisdom of the wise shall perish

chapters.n: By his Spirit he will reveal the secrets of his will—things no eye has seen or ear heard. This introduces the vision that follows.

f.w: eye has not seen, nor ear heard

chapters.n: Now Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon speak in their own voices, recording that they were “in the Spirit” on February 16, 1832. About a dozen others were in the room but did not see the vision.
By the Spirit’s power their eyes were opened and their minds enlightened to understand God’s things.
They saw things from before the world’s creation, ordained by the Father through his Only Begotten Son, who was with the Father from the beginning.

f.w: in the bosom of the Father

chapters.n: They testify of the Son—whom they saw and spoke with in the vision. Their witness is the fulness of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

f.w: whom we saw and with whom we conversed

chapters.n: The vision came while they were working on the Bible translation, at John 5:29.

f.w: the twenty-ninth verse of the fifth chapter of John

chapters.n: The verse speaks of the resurrection of those who hear the Son of Man’s voice.

f.w: the voice of the Son of Man

chapters.n: The inspired wording: the good come forth in the resurrection of the just, the evil in the resurrection of the unjust. The KJV reads “resurrection of life” and “resurrection of damnation.”

f.g: JST John 5:29 wording; compare KJV John 5:29.

chapters.n: This wording, given by the Spirit, made them marvel. It raised the question of how God judges people with such varied lives.
As they pondered, the Lord touched the eyes of their understanding and his glory shone around them. Pondering scripture often opens the door to revelation.

f.w: while we meditated upon these things

chapters.n: They saw the Son in glory at the Father’s right hand and received of his fulness.

f.w: on the right hand of the Father

chapters.n: They saw holy angels and the sanctified worshipping God and the Lamb forever.
After all the testimonies of Christ throughout history, theirs is the latest: “He lives!” One of the most beloved testimonies in the Restoration.
They saw him at God’s right hand and heard a voice testify that he is the Only Begotten of the Father.

f.w: the Only Begotten of the Father

chapters.n: By him, through him, and of him, worlds were created, and their inhabitants are begotten sons and daughters of God. Christ’s Atonement reaches many worlds.

f.w: the worlds are and were created
begotten sons and daughters unto God

chapters.n: They also saw an angel in authority before God who rebelled against the Son and was cast out of God’s presence.
He was called Perdition, for the heavens wept over him. He was Lucifer, a son of the morning.

f.g: Latin perditio, “loss” or “destruction”—the utterly lost one.

f.w: Lucifer, a son of the morning
f.g: Lucifer is Latin for “light-bearer.”

chapters.n: They watched in grief: he is fallen, fallen!
While still in the Spirit, they were told to write the vision. Satan, the old serpent, sought to take the kingdom of God and Christ.

f.w: that old serpent, even the devil

chapters.n: So he wars against the Saints and surrounds them.

f.w: he maketh war with the saints

chapters.n: They saw the suffering of those Satan overcame.
The Lord describes them: people who knew his power, partook of it, and then let the devil overcome them so that they denied the truth and defied God.
These are the sons of perdition; it would have been better for them never to have been born.

f.w: better for them never to have been born

chapters.n: They are “vessels of wrath,” destined to suffer God’s wrath with the devil and his angels.
For them there is no forgiveness in this world or the next.

f.w: no forgiveness in this world nor in the world to come

chapters.n: They denied the Holy Spirit after receiving it and denied the Son—as if crucifying him again and putting him to open shame. This requires full knowledge; it is not a sin of ignorance or weakness.

f.w: crucified him unto themselves and put him to an open shame

chapters.n: They will go into the lake of fire and brimstone with the devil.

f.w: the lake of fire and brimstone

chapters.n: They are the only ones the “second death”—final spiritual separation from God—will hold.
They alone will not be redeemed after suffering God’s wrath. Everyone else will eventually receive some degree of salvation.
All others will be resurrected through the triumph of the Lamb, slain for us and with the Father before the worlds were made.
This is the gospel—the glad tidings—declared to them by a voice from heaven.

f.g: Good news—the literal meaning of “gospel.”

chapters.n: Jesus came to be crucified, bear the world’s sins, and sanctify and cleanse it from all unrighteousness. A clear, compact definition of the gospel.

f.w: to bear the sins of the world

chapters.n: Through him all whom the Father gave him might be saved.
He glorifies the Father and saves all the works of his hands—except the sons of perdition, who deny the Son after the Father has revealed him.

f.w: saves all the works of his hands

chapters.n: He saves all except them. They go into “everlasting,” “endless,” “eternal” punishment, where the worm doesn’t die and the fire isn’t quenched—images Jesus used.

f.w: their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched

chapters.n: No one knows the end, place, or full torment of this condition.
It has not been, is not, and will not be revealed except to those who share in it.
Yet the Lord shows it in vision to many, then immediately closes the view.

f.g: Immediately.

chapters.n: Its full extent and misery are understood only by those ordained to this condemnation.
The voice told them to write; this ends the vision of the sufferings of the ungodly.
They now testify about those who will come forth in the resurrection of the just—the celestial.
These received the testimony of Jesus, believed, and were baptized by immersion—buried in water, symbolizing his burial—as he commanded.

f.w: baptized after the manner of his burial

chapters.n: By keeping the commandments they were cleansed, and received the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands from one with authority.

f.w: receive the Holy Spirit by the laying on of the hands

chapters.n: They overcome by faith and are sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, which the Father gives to all who are just and true.

f.g: The Holy Ghost confirming that ordinances and covenants are valid and accepted by God.

chapters.n: They are the Church of the Firstborn.

f.g: Those who inherit with Christ, the Firstborn, as joint-heirs.

chapters.n: The Father has given all things into their hands.

f.w: the Father has given all things

chapters.n: They are priests and kings who have received of his fulness and glory.
They are priests of the Most High after the order of Melchizedek—which is the order of Enoch and of the Only Begotten Son.
As scripture says, they are gods, sons of God—heirs who grow to become like their Father.
All things are theirs, and they are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s—quoting Paul.

f.w: all are theirs and they are Christ's, and Christ is God's

chapters.n: They will overcome all things.
So no one should boast in people, but in God, who will subdue all enemies.

f.w: let no man glory in man

chapters.n: They will live in the presence of God and Christ forever.
Christ will bring them with him when he comes to reign on earth.

f.w: whom he shall bring with him

chapters.n: They will have part in the first resurrection.
They will rise in the resurrection of the just.
They have come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the holiest heavenly place.

f.w: Mount Zion, and unto the city of the living God

chapters.n: They have joined countless angels and the general assembly of Enoch’s church and the Church of the Firstborn.
Their names are written in heaven, where God and Christ judge all.

f.w: whose names are written in heaven

chapters.n: They are just people made perfect through Jesus, mediator of the new covenant, who worked out a perfect atonement by shedding his own blood. Perfection comes through Christ, not by our own effort alone.

f.w: the mediator of the new covenant

chapters.n: Their bodies are celestial; their glory is like the sun—the glory of God, highest of all. The sun in the sky is a symbol of it.

f.w: whose glory is that of the sun

f.g: Serving as a type or symbol.

chapters.n: Next they saw the terrestrial world. Its glory differs from the celestial as the moon’s glory differs from the sun’s.

f.g: From Latin terra, “earth”; earthly, as opposed to heavenly (celestial).

chapters.n: These include those who died without law.
And spirits in prison to whom Christ preached, judged as people in the flesh are.

f.w: the spirits of men kept in prison

chapters.n: They rejected Jesus’s testimony in life but accepted it afterward. (Joseph Smith later learned that those who would have received the gospel had they had the chance may inherit the celestial kingdom—D&C 137.)

f.w: Who received not the testimony of Jesus in the flesh, but afterwards received it

chapters.n: They are honorable people who were blinded by others’ deceptions.
They receive of his glory but not his fulness.
They enjoy the Son’s presence, but not the fulness of the Father.
Their bodies are terrestrial, differing in glory as moon from sun.
These are not valiant in the testimony of Jesus, so they don’t receive the crown of God’s kingdom. A sobering reminder that lukewarm faith has consequences.

f.w: not valiant in the testimony of Jesus

chapters.n: This ends the vision of the terrestrial.
They saw the telestial glory—the lesser—differing from the terrestrial as the stars differ from the moon.

f.g: A word introduced in this revelation; it may echo Greek telos, “end,” but its exact origin is uncertain.

f.w: as the glory of the stars

chapters.n: These did not receive the gospel or the testimony of Jesus.
Yet they did not deny the Holy Spirit—which separates them from the sons of perdition.
They are thrust down to hell—in Latter-day Saint understanding, the spirit prison, a temporary state.
They won’t be redeemed from the devil until the last resurrection, after Christ finishes his work.
They don’t receive his fulness, but receive the Holy Spirit through those of the terrestrial kingdom.
The terrestrial in turn are ministered to by the celestial.
The telestial also receive ministering angels, for they are heirs of salvation.
Remarkably, the telestial glory surpasses all understanding. Even the lowest kingdom is glorious beyond mortal comprehension.
Only those to whom God reveals it know it.
The terrestrial glory exceeds the telestial in every way.
The celestial excels all, where God the Father reigns forever.
All things bow before his throne in humble reverence and glorify him forever.
Those in his presence are the Church of the Firstborn. They see as they are seen and know as they are known, having received his fulness and grace.

f.w: they see as they are seen, and know as they are known

chapters.n: He makes them equal in power, might, and dominion.
The celestial glory is one, as the sun’s glory is one.
The terrestrial glory is one, as the moon’s glory is one.
The telestial varies as stars differ in brightness; its inhabitants differ in glory.

f.w: as one star differs from another star in glory

chapters.n: These are those who claim to follow Paul, Apollos, or Cephas (Peter)—Paul’s description of divisive followers of men rather than Christ.

f.w: of Paul, and of Apollos, and of Cephas

chapters.n: They say they belong to various leaders—Christ, John, Moses, Elias, Esaias, Isaiah, Enoch—claiming labels without truly receiving the gospel.

f.g: Greek form of Isaiah, but here listed separately; D&C 84:11-13 mentions an Esaias from Abraham’s time.

chapters.n: They did not receive the gospel, the testimony of Jesus, the prophets, or the everlasting covenant.
They will not be gathered with the Saints to be caught up to meet Christ.
They include liars, sorcerers, adulterers, the sexually immoral, and lovers of lies.

f.w: whosoever loves and makes a lie

chapters.n: They suffer God’s wrath on earth.
They suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
They are cast down to hell until the fulness of times, when Christ has subdued all enemies and perfected his work.

f.w: subdued all enemies under his feet

chapters.n: Then Christ will deliver the kingdom to the Father spotless, saying he has overcome and trodden the winepress of God’s wrath alone—a picture of his solitary Atonement.
Then he will be crowned with glory to reign forever.
The telestial inhabitants are as countless as the stars or the sand on the seashore.

f.w: as the sand upon the seashore

chapters.n: Every knee will bow and every tongue confess to him on the throne.
All will be judged by their works and receive their own place in the mansions prepared.
They will be servants of the Most High, but cannot come where God and Christ dwell, “worlds without end.”

f.g: An idiom meaning forever.

chapters.n: The vision they were commanded to write now ends.
Yet the Lord showed them far more—great and marvelous mysteries surpassing understanding.

f.w: great and marvelous are the works of the Lord

chapters.n: They were commanded not to write those things, which are not lawful for man to utter.

f.w: not lawful for man to utter

chapters.n: Nor can humans convey them; they can be seen and understood only by the Holy Spirit, given to those who love God and purify themselves.

f.w: by the power of the Holy Spirit

chapters.n: God grants such people the privilege of seeing and knowing for themselves. The vision is an invitation, not just a report.
So that through the Spirit, while still mortal, they can be prepared to endure his presence in glory.
The vision ends with praise: glory, honor, and dominion to God and the Lamb forever.

f.w: to God and the Lamb be glory

chapters.n: While revising the Bible, Joseph Smith asked questions about the book of Revelation. The first: the “sea of glass” John saw before God’s throne is the earth in its future sanctified, immortal, eternal state.

f.g: Made holy.

chapters.n: The four beasts are symbolic figures describing heaven and the happiness of all God’s creatures—people, animals, birds. Spiritual things resemble physical ones and vice versa; even animals have spirits in the likeness of their bodies.

f.w: that which is spiritual being in the likeness of that which is temporal

chapters.n: The four beasts John saw were individual beings, but they represent the glory of whole classes of creatures in their eternal sphere and happiness.

f.g: Great happiness.

chapters.n: The beasts’ eyes symbolize light and knowledge; their wings symbolize power to move and act.
The twenty-four elders were faithful ministers who had died, belonged to the seven churches of Asia, and were in God’s paradise.
The book sealed with seven seals contains God’s will, mysteries, and works concerning the earth during its seven-thousand-year temporal existence—understood as the period since the Fall.

f.w: sealed on the back with seven seals

f.g: God’s management or plan.

chapters.n: Each seal represents a thousand years: the first seal the first thousand years, and so on to the seventh.

The four angels of Revelation 7 are sent from God with power over the earth’s four quarters to save or destroy. They carry the everlasting gospel to every nation, with power to seal to life or cast down.

The angel ascending from the east holds the seal of the living God over Israel’s twelve tribes and tells the four angels to wait until God’s servants are sealed. He is identified as an “Elias” who gathers Israel and restores all things.

f.w: the angel ascending from the east

f.g: A title for a forerunner or restorer, applied to several messengers.

chapters.n: These events take place in the sixth thousand-year period, at the opening of the sixth seal.
The 144,000 sealed from Israel’s tribes are high priests ordained to administer the gospel, called from every nation to bring all who will come into the Church of the Firstborn.

f.w: the one hundred and forty-four thousand

chapters.n: As God created the world in six days and sanctified the seventh, so at the start of the seventh thousand years he will sanctify the earth, complete salvation, and judge. The seven trumpets prepare the way for Christ’s coming.

f.w: on the seventh day he finished his work

chapters.n: The events of Revelation 9 occur after the seventh seal opens but before Christ comes. So the Second Coming follows a period of trouble within the seventh thousand years.
The little book John ate represents a mission and ordinance for him to gather Israel. John is an Elias, a restorer of all things.

f.w: the little book which was eaten by John

chapters.n: The two witnesses are two prophets raised up for the Jewish people in the last days, prophesying in Jerusalem after the Jews are gathered and the city is rebuilt.
The Lord addresses high priests gathered in Kirtland in March 1832. When first printed, some names in this revelation were replaced with code names to protect the Church’s business affairs.
He counsels them with wisdom concerning the matter they have brought before him.
The time has come to organize the storehouse for the poor in Kirtland and Zion. This led to the “United Firm,” which managed the Church’s storehouses and publishing.
It is to be a permanent order advancing the cause of salvation and glorifying the Father.

f.g: Embraced, committed to.

chapters.n: The goal: to be equal in heavenly and earthly things, for the sake of gaining heavenly things.

f.w: equal in the bonds of heavenly things

chapters.n: If they aren’t equal in earthly things, they can’t be equal in heavenly things. How we share material things shapes our spiritual readiness.

f.w: if ye are not equal in earthly things

chapters.n: To gain a place in the celestial world, they must prepare by obeying his commands.

f.w: a place in the celestial world

chapters.n: All should be done for God’s glory by those joined in this order.
Newel K. Whitney, Joseph Smith, and Sidney Rigdon are to go to Missouri and counsel with the Saints there. They traveled to Missouri in April 1832.

f.g: Meet and deliberate together.

chapters.n: Otherwise Satan will turn the Missouri Saints’ hearts away, blinding them to what is prepared for them. Tensions had grown between leaders in Ohio and Missouri.
They must organize by an everlasting covenant that cannot be broken.

f.g: A formal, binding agreement.

chapters.n: Whoever breaks it loses office and standing and is delivered to the “buffetings of Satan” until redemption—left without God’s protection to experience the adversary’s attacks.

f.g: Buffet = strike repeatedly.

chapters.n: This is the preparation, foundation, and example to help them keep his commands.

f.g: Example or pattern.

chapters.n: Through God’s care, despite coming hardships, the Church may stand independent of all other powers under heaven. Self-reliance is a spiritual principle.

f.g: God’s care and guidance.

chapters.n: So they may receive their crown and rule over many kingdoms. The Lord is the Holy One of Zion, who established Adam-ondi-Ahman.

f.g: The place where Adam blessed his posterity; later identified with a site in Daviess County, Missouri.

chapters.n: He appointed Michael—Adam—as their prince and gave him the keys of salvation under the direction of the Holy One, who has no beginning or end.

f.g: Michael is Adam’s premortal name.

f.w: without beginning of days or end of life

chapters.n: They are still little children who don’t yet understand the blessings the Father has prepared.
They can’t bear everything now, but be of good cheer—he will lead them along. The kingdom and eternity’s riches are theirs.
Whoever receives all things with thankfulness will be made glorious, and earthly blessings will be added a hundredfold. Gratitude itself is a path to glory.
Obey, says the Redeemer, the “Son Ahman,” who prepares all things. “Ahman” was revealed as a name for God, making “Son Ahman” a title of Christ.

f.g: A title for Jesus Christ; Ahman is given as a name of God the Father.

chapters.n: They are the Church of the Firstborn; he will take them up in a cloud and appoint each person his portion.

f.w: take you up in a cloud

chapters.n: The faithful and wise steward will inherit all things.
Jared Carter, who had already served a mission in the East, is called to go again, traveling town to town with the priesthood authority he received at his ordination to share the restored gospel.

f.g: The eastern United States and Canada—“countries” here means regions or districts, not nations.

chapters.n: He will not go alone: the Holy Ghost, the Comforter, will teach him what is true and even guide where he should travel next.

f.g: To which place; where.

chapters.n: If he stays faithful, the Lord will again reward him with converts—pictured as bundles of harvested grain carried home with joy.

f.g: Bundles of harvested grain; here a symbol of the people brought into the gospel through a missionary’s labor.

chapters.n: The Savior closes with tender encouragement: be glad and don’t be afraid. The one sending Jared is Jesus Christ himself.
Stephen Burnett, a young convert from Ohio, is called to share the gospel with anyone within reach of his voice. The command echoes the Savior’s charge to his ancient apostles.

f.w: preach the gospel to every creature

chapters.n: The Lord grants his wish for a companion and names Eden Smith to serve with him. Missionaries traditionally went out in pairs.
The direction they travel doesn’t matter—north, south, east, or west—because wherever they go there are people who need the gospel. Sometimes the Lord leaves the choice to us.

f.g: You cannot go wrong; any direction is acceptable.

chapters.n: Their message is simple: tell what they have heard, what they sincerely believe, and what they know is true. A missionary’s testimony is built from these three.
The call comes from Jesus Christ, their Redeemer—so it carries his authority and his promise of help.

This revelation was first given to Jesse Gause, a counselor to Joseph Smith. When he left the Church, Frederick G. Williams was called in his place and his name was put into the text. He is to serve as a high priest and counselor to the Prophet.

f.g: A physician from Ohio; he served in the First Presidency from 1833 to 1837.

chapters.n: The keys of the kingdom—the authority to direct the Lord’s work on earth—belong to the Presidency of the High Priesthood, which today we call the First Presidency.
The Lord promises to bless both Joseph and his counselor if the counselor is faithful—in giving counsel, in praying constantly (aloud and silently, in public and alone), and in sharing the gospel.
Faithful service in these ways is the greatest good he can do for others, and it brings glory to the Lord.
A beloved charge for every disciple: help those who are weak, lift up the discouraged, and strengthen those who are ready to give up. The phrase comes from Isaiah’s comfort to tired Israel.

f.g: To come to the aid of; to help in time of need.

f.w: lift up the hands which hang down

chapters.n: Enduring faithfully to the end leads to immortality and eternal life in the Father’s house, where Christ has prepared a place for his followers.

f.g: Dwelling places.

chapters.n: The revelation ends with Christ’s title Alpha and Omega—the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet—meaning he is the beginning and the end of all things.

f.g: First and last letters of the Greek alphabet.

chapters.n: Joseph Smith had traveled to Missouri, where tension between him and Bishop Edward Partridge had been healed. The Lord tells these leaders that because they forgave each other, he forgives them.
Some had sinned seriously—and in truth everyone had sinned. The Lord warns them to stop sinning from now on, or painful consequences will follow.

f.g: Severe, painful.

chapters.n: A key principle: the more light and knowledge we receive, the more God expects of us. Sinning against greater light brings greater accountability.

f.w: unto whom much is given much is required

chapters.n: They had asked for revelations and received them. Ignoring those revelations makes them transgressors, because God’s law carries consequences for disobedience.
The command to “watch” applies to everyone, because Satan is expanding his influence and spiritual darkness is spreading.

f.g: Be alert and on guard.

chapters.n: God is displeased with the world’s wickedness. The wording echoes the Psalms’ lament that people have turned aside from the right path.
Christ offers complete forgiveness: go and sin no more. But someone who returns to sin brings the weight of earlier sins back on himself.

f.w: go your ways and sin no more

chapters.n: The Lord now gives a new commandment so they can clearly understand what he wants of them.
Put another way, he is giving practical directions for how to act—directions meant to lead to their salvation.
One of the most quoted verses in the D&C: when we obey, the Lord binds himself to keep his promises; when we don’t, we have no claim on them.
Nine leaders in Ohio and Missouri are to be joined by a formal covenant, later called the United Firm, to manage Church business. Breaking it by sin would bring immediate judgment.

f.w: bound together by a bond and covenant
f.g: This organization became known as the United Firm (or United Order), formed to manage the Church’s publishing and storehouse operations.
Responsibilities entrusted to someone to manage for the Lord.

chapters.n: Their purpose was to care for the poor and manage the bishops’ work in both Missouri (Zion) and Ohio (Kirtland).
Kirtland, Ohio, is dedicated as a stake of Zion—a support for the central gathering place in Missouri.

f.g: Like the stakes that hold up a tent, a stake strengthens and extends Zion.

chapters.n: Zion must grow in beauty and holiness, spread out, and strengthen its stakes. Isaiah’s image of Zion putting on beautiful clothes pictures God’s people rising to their full potential.
The leaders are commanded to enter this covenant and carry it out according to the Lord’s laws.
The Lord assures them that this arrangement is wise and for their own benefit.
Members of the firm were to have equal claim on its resources, each according to legitimate needs and wants—not greed, but what is just.

f.w: inasmuch as his wants are just

chapters.n: The goal was to build up the Church: each person develops and multiplies his talents and contributes the gains to the Lord’s storehouse for everyone’s benefit.
The spirit of the order: look out for your neighbor’s good, and do everything with your focus fixed only on glorifying God.

f.w: an eye single to the glory of God
f.g: Undivided focus; motives pointed entirely toward God.

f.w: seeking the interest of his neighbor

chapters.n: This order was meant to last for them and their successors—as long as they did not sin.
Anyone who breaks the covenant and hardens his heart will face Church discipline and be left without God’s protection from Satan until the day of redemption.

f.g: Being struck or harassed by Satan without God’s shielding.

chapters.n: Borrowing a phrase from Jesus’s parable, the Lord counsels them to deal wisely and peaceably with people of the world who hold wealth, so they won’t be destroyed by them.

f.g: Worldly wealth; “mammon” is an Aramaic word for riches.

chapters.n: They must not seek revenge—judgment belongs to God. He leaves them with his peace and continued blessing.
The kingdom is still theirs and will be forever, if they remain steadfast. It is a hopeful promise after the earlier warnings.
Adding to earlier Church laws, the Lord explains how to care for women and children who have lost husbands or fathers—a concern of God’s people in every age.
Wives have a right to be supported by their husbands while the husbands live. If a woman is widowed and remains faithful, she keeps full fellowship in the Church.

f.g: A rightful demand; a just right to receive something.

chapters.n: If she is not faithful she loses Church fellowship, yet she may still keep her land and home as the civil law allows. The Church did not strip widows of property.

f.g: Land assigned to members under the law of consecration.

chapters.n: Every child has a right to be provided for by his or her parents until reaching adulthood.

f.g: Old enough to be legally an adult.

chapters.n: When parents can’t provide an inheritance, children then have a claim on the Church—that is, on the Lord’s storehouse.
Members’ consecrated offerings keep the storehouse supplied, so widows, orphans, and the poor are cared for. True religion has always included this.
This revelation came over two days in Kirtland as Joseph Smith and six elders, recently returned from missions, prayed together in unity. Joseph later called it a revelation on priesthood.
The Lord’s purpose for his latter-day Church: to restore scattered Israel, as the prophets foretold, and gather the Saints to Mount Zion—the New Jerusalem.
The city is to begin at a temple site in Independence, Missouri, which Joseph Smith and others had dedicated in August 1831 under the Lord’s direction.

f.g: A site in Independence, Jackson County, Missouri, dedicated August 3, 1831.

chapters.n: The New Jerusalem will be built as the Saints gather, starting at the temple site. The Lord says the temple will be raised “in this generation.”

f.g: Built, raised up.

chapters.n: A house of the Lord will be built, and his glory will rest on it as a cloud—like the cloud that filled the ancient tabernacle and Solomon’s temple. The Saints were later driven from Jackson County, and the Lord addressed that delay in D&C 124:49-51.

f.w: a cloud shall rest upon it

chapters.n: The revelation now traces the priesthood back in time, starting with the “sons of Moses”—those who hold the priesthood Moses received from his father-in-law, Jethro.

f.g: A priest of Midian and Moses’s father-in-law.

chapters.n: Jethro received the priesthood from Caleb—not the Caleb of Joshua’s day, but an earlier person known only from this revelation.

f.g: Known only from this list; not the same as Caleb son of Jephunneh in Numbers.

chapters.n: Caleb received it from Elihu. These names show a real, unbroken chain of authority passed by the laying on of hands.

f.g: An ancient priesthood holder known from this revelation.

chapters.n: Elihu received it from Jeremy, another figure otherwise unknown in scripture.

f.g: An English form of the name Jeremiah; this man is not the prophet Jeremiah.

chapters.n: Jeremy received the priesthood from Gad—again someone known only from this line, not the son of Jacob or the prophet Gad of David’s time.
Gad received it from Esaias, the next link back toward Abraham.

f.g: Greek form of Isaiah; this Esaias lived in Abraham’s time and is not the prophet Isaiah.

chapters.n: Esaias received the priesthood directly from God—a reminder that all true priesthood authority begins with him.
Esaias was a contemporary of Abraham and received a blessing from him, linking this line to the great patriarch.
Abraham received the priesthood from Melchizedek, the righteous king of Salem, whose own authority came down through his ancestors back to Noah.
From Noah the line goes back to Enoch through their family line.
And from Enoch back to Abel, who was murdered by Cain’s plot. Abel received the priesthood from his father Adam, the first man, at God’s command.

f.w: Adam, who was the first man

chapters.n: This higher priesthood continues in God’s true church in every age. It is “without beginning of days or end of years” because it is eternal, like God himself.

f.w: without beginning of days or end of years
f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation of Hebrews 7:3 clarifies that this phrase describes the priesthood, not Melchizedek himself.

chapters.n: The Lord also gave a priesthood to Aaron and his descendants—the Aaronic or lesser priesthood. It too continues alongside the higher priesthood “after the holiest order of God.”
The higher (Melchizedek) priesthood administers the full gospel and holds the key to knowing God—the deepest truths of his kingdom.

f.w: the key of the knowledge of God

f.g: Sacred truths known only by revelation.

chapters.n: Through its ordinances—like baptism, confirmation, and temple covenants—God’s power to make people godly is shown and given.

f.g: The divine power that makes people more like God.

chapters.n: Without those ordinances and proper authority, that power isn’t made manifest to mortal people. This is one reason the Restoration of priesthood mattered so much.

f.g: In mortal life.

chapters.n: Without this power, no one can see God the Father and live. Priesthood ordinances prepare people to enter God’s presence.
Moses taught this clearly to Israel in the wilderness and worked hard to make his people holy so they could see God.
But Israel hardened their hearts and could not bear God’s presence, so he swore they would not enter his “rest” in the wilderness—the fulness of his glory.
So God removed Moses and the higher priesthood from among the people as a whole.

f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation of Exodus 34:1-2 adds that the second set of tablets omitted the higher priesthood ordinances.

chapters.n: The lesser priesthood remained. It holds the key of the ministering of angels and the “preparatory gospel”—the first steps that prepare people for more.

f.g: The basic gospel of faith, repentance, and baptism that prepares for greater light.

chapters.n: That preparatory gospel—repentance, baptism, forgiveness, and the law of Moses—stayed with Aaron’s line until John the Baptist, who was filled with the Holy Ghost even before birth.

f.g: The outward rules of the law of Moses, focused on physical observances.

f.w: filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb

chapters.n: John was baptized as a child and, when eight days old, was ordained by an angel to prepare the way for Christ, overthrowing the corrupt religious power of his day.

f.w: make straight the way of the Lord
in whose hand is given all power

chapters.n: Elders and bishops are offices that grow out of, and belong to, the higher priesthood.

f.g: Parts attached to a larger whole; offices that branch from the priesthood.

chapters.n: Teachers and deacons are offices belonging to the lesser (Aaronic) priesthood, first given to Aaron and his sons.
Returning to the “sons of Moses”: priesthood holders of both orders will offer an acceptable offering in the Lord’s house to be built on the consecrated site.
These priesthood holders will be filled with God’s glory in his house on Mount Zion. The Lord tells the elders that they are these “sons of Moses and of Aaron.”
Those who faithfully receive both priesthoods and “magnify” their callings are made holy by the Spirit, even to the renewing of their bodies.

f.g: Making a calling great by serving with full effort and faith.

chapters.n: They become heirs of Moses, Aaron, and Abraham—God’s covenant people and chosen ones.
Here begins the “oath and covenant of the priesthood”: those who receive the priesthood receive Christ himself.
Receiving the Lord’s servants means receiving the Lord who sent them.

f.w: he that receiveth my servants receiveth me

chapters.n: And receiving Christ means receiving the Father who sent him.
Receiving the Father brings his kingdom—indeed “all that my Father hath.” It is the greatest promise God can make: to share everything he has.
This is what the oath and covenant of the priesthood means. God promises with an oath; the person covenants to be faithful.
Everyone who receives the priesthood receives this covenant from the Father, and he will never break it or move away from it.
But someone who receives it and then breaks it by turning completely away will not be forgiven, in this world or the next—a very serious warning about total, willful apostasy.

f.g: Completely abandons it—not merely stumbling, but fully and knowingly turning away.

chapters.n: Sorrow awaits those who refuse this priesthood. The Lord personally confirms it on the men present and assigns angels to watch over them.
A new section begins: be careful of yourselves and pay close attention to the words that lead to eternal life.
We are to live by every word that comes from God—quoting what Jesus told Satan in the wilderness.

f.w: every word that proceedeth forth from the mouth of God

chapters.n: A chain of truths: God’s word is truth, truth is light, and light is Spirit—the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
This Spirit, often called the Light of Christ, gives light to every person born. Those who listen to it receive more light.

f.w: giveth light to every man that cometh into the world

chapters.n: Listening to the Spirit leads a person to God the Father.
The Father teaches such people about the covenant he has renewed with the Saints—given not only for them but for the blessing of the whole world.

f.w: for the sake of the whole world

chapters.n: Without that covenant, the world lies in sin, groaning in darkness and bondage.

f.g: Moans in distress.

chapters.n: The sign of this bondage is that people do not come to Christ.
Anyone who does not come unto Christ remains captive to sin. Christ alone frees us.
Those who reject Christ’s voice don’t truly know it and aren’t his. His sheep know his voice.
This is how to tell the righteous from the wicked—and why the world groans under sin even now.
The Lord turns to the Church: their minds had been darkened by unbelief and by treating sacred things too casually.

f.g: Took casually; did not value as sacred.

chapters.n: That vanity and unbelief had put the whole Church under condemnation.

f.g: Emptiness, pride, or worthless pursuits.

chapters.n: This condemnation rests on all the children of Zion, without exception.

It will remain until they repent and remember the “new covenant,” the Book of Mormon, and the earlier commandments—not just talking about them but living them. Church leaders have repeatedly applied this to how members value the Book of Mormon.

f.w: the new covenant, even the Book of Mormon
not only to say, but to do

chapters.n: They must produce fruit worthy of the Father’s kingdom, or else judgment will come on Zion’s people.

f.g: Fruit that is fitting or worthy.

chapters.n: The Lord will not let his people pollute the holy land he has promised them.
To those who heard these words directly, he promises blessing if they receive them.
Their sins are forgiven on condition that they stay serious and prayerful and bear testimony to the world of what has been revealed to them.

f.g: Seriousness and reverence of mind.

chapters.n: They must take the gospel into all the world, and where they can’t go personally, they must send others.

f.w: go ye into all the world

chapters.n: Christ calls these elders his apostles, God’s high priests, gifts from the Father—and his friends.

f.w: whom my Father hath given me

chapters.n: As with his ancient apostles, anyone who believes their words and is baptized for the remission of sins will receive the Holy Ghost.

f.w: baptized by water for the remission of sins

chapters.n: Miraculous signs will follow those who believe—an echo of the Savior’s words at the end of Mark.

f.w: these signs shall follow them that believe

chapters.n: Believers will do many wonderful works in Christ’s name.
They will cast out evil spirits in his name.
They will heal the sick in his name.
They will heal blindness and deafness, as Jesus himself did.

f.w: open the eyes of the blind

chapters.n: Those unable to speak will speak.

f.g: Unable to speak (not a comment on intelligence).

chapters.n: Poison given to them will not hurt them.
Even snake venom will not harm them.
But they must not boast of these miracles or show them off to the world. Gifts of the Spirit are for blessing and saving people, not for display.

f.w: for your profit and for salvation

chapters.n: Those who reject the message and refuse baptism will be “damned”—stopped in their progress—and cannot enter the Father’s kingdom.

f.g: Condemned; stopped from progressing to God’s presence.

chapters.n: This command is in force from this moment for the whole world. The gospel is for everyone who has not yet received it.
Even those who have the kingdom must be called to repentance: some Saints for their unbelief, and members in Zion for rebelling against the elders when they visited earlier.

f.g: Scolded, rebuked.

chapters.n: From now on Christ calls them friends. He wants them to travel and preach in his power, as his disciples did when he was on earth.
Those early disciples went without money bags, food sacks, or extra coats, trusting God completely.

f.g: A money pouch or a traveling bag for food.

chapters.n: They are sent to test the world. And a worker deserves to be supported by those he serves.

f.g: Test.

f.w: the laborer is worthy of his hire

chapters.n: Faithful missionaries are promised strength of mind and body, and God will notice every detail of their lives—even a single hair. They will not go hungry or thirsty.

f.w: a hair of his head shall not fall to the ground unnoticed

chapters.n: So don’t worry about tomorrow—about food, drink, or clothing.

f.w: take ye no thought for the morrow
f.g: Don’t be anxious about tomorrow.

chapters.n: Look at the wildflowers: they don’t work or weave, yet they’re dressed more beautifully than any kingdom’s glory.

f.w: consider the lilies of the field
toil not, neither do they spin
f.g: Don’t labor or spin thread to make cloth.

chapters.n: Your Father in Heaven knows you need all these things.
So let tomorrow take care of itself.
Don’t prepare speeches ahead of time; instead, constantly store up the words of life in your mind, and you’ll be given what to say at the very moment it’s needed.

f.w: treasure up in your minds continually the words of life
it shall be given you in the very hour

chapters.n: This applies to everyone called to the ministry: from now on, go without purse or scrip when proclaiming the gospel.
Missionaries are sent to call the world to repent of its wrongdoing and to warn of a coming judgment.

f.g: Correct, rebuke.

chapters.n: A tender promise: Christ will go before them, be on their right and left, put his Spirit in their hearts, and surround them with angels to hold them up.

f.w: I will go before your face

chapters.n: Whoever welcomes them welcomes Christ, and will feed, clothe, and support them.
Those who help them will surely be rewarded.

f.w: shall in nowise lose his reward

chapters.n: Those who refuse to help are not true disciples; caring for the Lord’s servants is a mark of discipleship.

f.w: by this you may know my disciples

chapters.n: If someone rejects them, they should leave privately, wash their feet as a witness before God, and not return to that person. This is a solemn act, not a casual gesture.
They are to do the same in any village or city that rejects them.
Still, they must search diligently and not hold back. Sorrow comes to any home or town that rejects them and their testimony of Christ.

f.g: Don’t hold back; give full effort.

chapters.n: The warning is repeated for emphasis—rejecting Christ’s witnesses is serious.
The Almighty has laid his hand on the nations to discipline them for their wickedness.

f.g: Punish, as with a whip.

chapters.n: Plagues will continue until the Lord finishes his work, which he will cut short in righteousness for the sake of his elect.
In the end, everyone who remains will know the Lord, from least to greatest. They will see eye to eye and together sing a new song.

f.w: from the least unto the greatest

chapters.n: The new song begins: the Lord has restored Zion and redeemed Israel by his grace, fulfilling the faith and covenants of their ancestors.

f.g: Being chosen by God’s grace, not by our own merit.

chapters.n: Satan is bound, time as we know it ends, and all things are gathered in one in Christ. Zion comes down from heaven and rises up from the earth to meet it.
